hypotheses.title: Literature Mining: PubMed Drug-Disease Hypothesis Extraction
hypotheses.rationale: Novel drug-disease hypotheses exist in published literature but aren't in DRKG. LLMs can extract these relationships at scale. This is fundamentally different from graph-based methods and could work for truly untreated diseases.
steps: Step 1: For each zero-treatment disease (from h90), query PubMed for recent papers
Step 2: Use Claude to extract: disease mechanisms, affected genes/pathways, proposed treatments
Step 3: For proposed treatments, search for supporting evidence (other papers, trials)
Step 4: Score hypotheses by: mechanism plausibility, evidence strength, safety profile
Step 5: Validate top predictions against clinical trials database
Success criteria: Generate predictions for 50%+ of zero-treatment diseases

hypotheses.title: Category Boundary Refinement
hypotheses.rationale: h175 revealed category boundaries matter more than drug overlap suggests. The current keyword-based categorization may be suboptimal. Could data-driven clustering (based on drug overlap) create better categories?
steps: Cluster diseases by drug treatment overlap (Jaccard)
Compare clusters to current keyword-based categories
Test if cluster-based boosting outperforms category-based

hypotheses.title: Cross-Category Disease Recall Enhancement
hypotheses.rationale: h277 revealed cross-category diseases (diabetic nephropathy, lupus nephritis) have 0% prediction precision because the kNN model doesn't recommend correct drugs for them at all. This is a recall problem, not precision. Could we expand the kNN neighbor search to include diseases from related categories?
steps: Step 1: Identify cross-category diseases in GT (diabetic nephropathy, lupus nephritis)
Step 2: For these diseases, also search kNN neighbors in the "parent" category
Step 3: E.g., for diabetic nephropathy, include diabetes (metabolic) neighbors + nephropathy (renal) neighbors
Step 4: Evaluate if this improves R@30 for cross-category diseases
Success criteria: >20% R@30 for cross-category diseases

hypotheses.title: Build Comprehensive Drug/Disease ID Mapping Infrastructure
hypotheses.description: Data infrastructure task: The ID format mismatch (CHEBI/MONDO/UMLS in GT vs DrugBank/CHEMBL/MESH in reference data) has been a persistent blocker for 20+ hypotheses. Build a comprehensive bidirectional mapping using PubChem and UniProt APIs. This unblocks target/pathway analysis, LINCS integration, and external dataset connections. Supersedes h301.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Using PubChem's REST API to map DrugBank→PubChem CID→CHEBI→CHEMBL, and disease ontology crossrefs to map MESH→MONDO→UMLS, we can achieve >80% coverage for drugs and >60% for diseases, unblocking the entire class of target/pathway hypotheses.
steps: Step 1: Drug ID mapping via PubChem REST API: for each DrugBank drug, query PubChem for cross-references (CHEBI, CHEMBL, CAS, InChIKey)
Step 2: Batch queries (PubChem allows 5 requests/sec): process in batches with rate limiting
Step 3: Disease ID mapping: use MONDO xrefs (already have mondo_to_mesh.json), extend with UMLS and DOID
Step 4: Download OBO files for disease ontologies if needed for cross-reference extraction
Step 5: Save unified mapping files: data/reference/id_mappings/drug_id_map.json, disease_id_map.json
Step 6: Report coverage: what % of GT drugs now have DrugBank IDs? What % of GT diseases have MESH IDs?
Step 7: Re-evaluate previously blocked hypotheses that needed ID mapping
Step 8: Success criteria: >80% drug ID coverage, >60% disease ID coverage
hypotheses.rationale: Data infrastructure task: The ID format mismatch (CHEBI/MONDO/UMLS in GT vs DrugBank/CHEMBL/MESH in reference data) has been a persistent blocker for 20+ hypotheses. Build a comprehensive bidirectional mapping using PubChem and UniProt APIs. This unblocks target/pathway analysis, LINCS integration, and external dataset connections. Supersedes h301.

hypotheses.title: [RYLAND] Gene Expression Disease Signatures from GEO/ARCHS4
hypotheses.description: Collaboration prep: Download disease gene expression signatures from GEO/ARCHS4 to complement our KG-based approach. ARCHS4 contains uniformly processed RNA-seq data from >1M samples. Disease signatures (differentially expressed genes) provide an orthogonal signal to KG structure for drug-disease matching. Ryland's transcriptomics expertise can guide which signatures are most informative. Supersedes h55 and h172.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Disease gene expression signatures from ARCHS4, combined with LINCS drug signatures (h404/h406), will enable signature-matching drug repurposing: drugs whose transcriptional effect reverses the disease signature are therapeutic candidates. This is the CMap/AMVL approach that achieved SOTA in 2025 literature.
steps: Step 1: Download ARCHS4 human gene expression matrix from https://maayanlab.cloud/archs4/download.html
Step 2: Identify disease-relevant samples using metadata (disease labels, tissue types)
Step 3: Compute disease signatures: differentially expressed genes (disease vs healthy) for diseases in our GT
Step 4: Coverage: how many of our 3K+ diseases have expression signatures in ARCHS4?
Step 5: For covered diseases, compute reversal score: does the drug signature (from L1000) reverse the disease signature?
Step 6: Evaluate: do high reversal scores correlate with GT drug-disease pairs?
Step 7: Discuss methodology with Ryland — his spatial transcriptomics perspective on which signatures are meaningful
Step 8: Success criteria: Reversal score has >1.5x enrichment in GT pairs vs random

Ryland's transcriptomics expertise can guide which signatures are most informative. Supersedes h55 and h172.

hypotheses.title: Migraine Drug Coverage Gap: Why Are CGRP Antibodies Not Predicted?
hypotheses.description: h492 found 6 migraine drugs missing including 3 CGRP antibodies (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab) and prophylactic drugs (propranolol, topiramate, amitriptyline). None appear in top-30 predictions. This suggests the kNN model struggles with diseases that have mechanistically diverse treatment options (acute triptans vs preventive beta-blockers vs CGRP antibodies). Understanding WHY could reveal a structural model limitation.
steps: Examine migraine's kNN neighborhood - what diseases are nearest?
Check which migraine drugs ARE in top-30 and which drug classes are missing
Determine if preventive vs acute treatments have different kNN coverage
Generalize: are multi-mechanism diseases systematically underpredicted?

hypotheses.title: Drug Class Expansion for Migraine: Predict All Triptans and CGRPs
hypotheses.description: Migraine is a therapeutic island where kNN fails (0% holdout). But 7 of 35 GT drugs are triptans, 3 are CGRP antibodies. If the system knew ONE triptan treats migraine, it could predict ALL triptans. ATC class-based expansion could generate predictions independent of kNN. Requires mapping ATC classes to drug IDs.
steps: For each island disease, identify the dominant drug classes in GT
Map ATC L4/L5 classes to all drugs in the system
If any drug from class X is in GT for disease Y, predict all other class X drugs for Y
Compute holdout precision of class expansion predictions
Compare with kNN top-30 for these diseases

hypotheses.title: CS GT Gap Expansion for Remaining 15 PLAUSIBLE Diseases
hypotheses.description: h669 identified 27 GENUINE and 15 PLAUSIBLE CS disease-CS pairs. The 12 GENUINE CS GT gaps were filled. The 15 PLAUSIBLE diseases (familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, familial mediterranean fever, psoriasis vulgaris, scleroderma, hidradenitis suppurativa, pityriasis rubra pilaris, pruritus, pruritus ani, corneal ulcer, retinitis, bronchiectasis, empyema, laryngitis, silicosis, SSc-ILD) could potentially have CS added to GT after more careful literature review.

Classify: FDA-approved, guideline-recommended, RCT-supported, expert opinion only
Add pairs with FDA/guideline/RCT support to expanded GT
Measure holdout impact

hypotheses.title: Expanded GT → Internal GT Promotion: Add High-Confidence DRKG Drug-Disease Pairs
hypotheses.description: h683 found 2,446 drugs with DRKG embeddings and expanded GT entries but NOT in internal GT. These drugs CAN'T be predicted currently because the kNN model only recommends drugs from the training set. If we promoted high-confidence expanded GT entries (from DRKG treatment edges, not co-occurrence) to internal GT, these drugs could enter the prediction pool. Most impactful drugs: rifampicin (84 diseases), aciclovir (84), isotretinoin (80), propofol (87). Needs careful curation to avoid adding noise.
steps: Identify top 50 drugs by expanded GT count that have DRKG embeddings
Filter out non-therapeutic compounds (oxygen, ethanol, metabolites)
For remaining drugs, verify they're real therapeutics with specific indications
Add verified drug-disease pairs to internal GT (Every Cure format)
Run holdout evaluation to measure impact on predictions

hypotheses.title: GT Expansion for Single-Indication Drugs: Can Literature Mining Rescue the 478 Invisible GT Drugs?
hypotheses.description: h703 found that 478 GT drugs (41.3%) never generate predictions because they treat only 1-2 diseases (mean GT=1.3). The kNN model needs GT≥3 for 83.6% prediction rate. For these drugs, systematic literature mining (ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, drug labels) could identify additional indications that would bring them above the critical mass threshold. Even adding 1 more indication to GT=1 drugs doubles their prediction rate (31.8%→59.1%). This is the highest-ROI GT expansion possible. Focus on drug classes with many invisible members: biologics (54), antihypertensives (20), antibiotics (17).
hypotheses.hypothesis: Literature mining can identify additional indications for single-GT drugs, raising them above the prediction threshold.
steps: Prioritize the 180 GT=1 drugs that have embeddings but don't predict
For top 50 by DRKG connectivity, search ClinicalTrials.gov for additional indications
Add validated pairs to expanded GT
Re-evaluate prediction rate change

hypotheses.title: Disease Subtype-to-Parent Mapping Infrastructure: Transfer Predictions from DRKG Parent Diseases
hypotheses.rationale: h707 showed 9 diseases without DRKG embeddings have clear parent diseases with embeddings. 5/9 have medically sound prediction transfers (HoFH→FH: 100% GT captured, Esophageal SCC→esophageal cancer: 75% GT). This requires building a disease subtype→parent mapping and fallback prediction mechanism.
steps: Create DISEASE_SUBTYPE_MAPPING dict mapping child disease IDs to parent disease IDs
Implement fallback: if disease has no embedding, try parent disease predictions
Annotate transferred predictions with 'transferred_from_parent' flag
Validate against GT for the 9 candidate diseases
Assess whether transferred predictions should get lower confidence tier

hypotheses.title: Biomarker-Matched Targeted Therapy Rescue: Use DRKG Mutation Edges for Cancer Drug Matching
hypotheses.rationale: h718 showed targeted therapy fails kNN transfer because biomarkers (BRAF V600E, HER2+, BRCA1/2) are cancer-subtype-specific. DRKG contains Gene:Mutation→Disease edges and Drug→Gene:Target edges. If a targeted therapy drug targets Gene X, and holdout disease has Gene X mutation, this is a biologically-grounded match that doesn't depend on kNN neighbors. This would be a fundamentally different signal from kNN and could rescue high-quality targeted therapy predictions.
steps: Extract Drug→Gene:Target edges from DRKG for CANCER_TARGETED_THERAPY drugs
Extract Gene:Mutation→Disease edges from DRKG for cancer diseases
Compute drug-disease matches via shared gene targets
Check if biomarker-matched predictions have higher holdout precision than kNN
If validated, implement as targeted_therapy_biomarker_match sub-reason

Running full mining would: (1) find more GT gaps in LOW tier (could promote some), (2) find more inverse indications, (3) enable evidence-based tier adjustments across all tiers. Rate limiting: ~2s per fresh query × 13,500 = ~7.5 hours.

Batch run literature mining on FILTER predictions (7,288 predictions, ~4 hours)
Analyze GT gaps by tier - are there STRONG evidence LOW predictions that should be MEDIUM?
Analyze inverse indications found - add confirmed to safety filters

hypotheses.title: Default Freq5 Mechanism Low-Score Demotion: Score<1.0 is 31.7% Holdout
hypotheses.rationale: h742 analysis found default_freq5_mechanism at score<1.0 has 31.7% ± 6.4% (n=18.6/seed) — borderline LOW vs MEDIUM. z-score vs MEDIUM avg (47.7%): z = (31.7-47.7)/6.4 = -2.5 below MEDIUM. This subset may warrant demotion. However, mechanism support makes these higher-quality than pure frequency preds. Need to check: (1) what drugs/diseases are in this group, (2) whether the mechanism signal compensates for low kNN score.
steps: Analyze drugs/diseases in freq5_mech score<1.0 group
Check if these are systematic errors or genuine borderline
If demotion warranted, implement score<1.0 demotion for freq5_mech
Run holdout validation
Estimate MEDIUM precision impact
hypotheses.findings: h746 INCONCLUSIVE: default_freq5_mechanism score gradient analysis. Score < 0.75: 22.0% ± 3.7% (n=10.4/seed) — clearly below MEDIUM but n too small for reliable demotion (only 24 predictions). Score 0.75-1.0: ~44% holdout — at MEDIUM level, should NOT be demoted. Score >= 1.0: 56.1% ± 5.6% (n=28.2/seed) — HIGH quality, but promoting would hurt MEDIUM (-1.6pp) by removing good predictions. Total freq5_mech only 204 predictions (minor sub-rule). h742 estimate of 31.7% for score<1.0 was driven by score<0.75 (22%) dragging down the average; score 0.75-1.0 is genuinely MEDIUM (~44%). No action taken — effect too small and unreliable.
hypotheses.result_metric: No change — inconclusive

hypotheses.title: Literature Mining Expansion: Mine ALL 13K+ Predictions for Evidence Tier Modifiers
hypotheses.rationale: h732 validated literature evidence as a tier modifier: STRONG→HIGH (60.2%), WEAK/NO→LOW (10.4%). Currently only 590 of ~13K predictions have been mined. Full mining would identify many more STRONG and WEAK predictions, further improving tier separation. Based on h731 evidence distribution: ~10% STRONG, ~15% WEAK/NO. Full mining could promote ~130 to HIGH and demote ~200 to LOW. Main bottleneck: PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov API rate limits.

Mine HIGH and GOLDEN predictions for quality audit
Analyze evidence distribution across tiers
Implement results as tier modifiers
Run holdout validation with full evidence data

Category-stratified splitting would ensure each seed has proportional GI representation. This could reduce variance for per-category holdout estimates. Already noted as structural issue in h617 (HIGH ±13.5% is irreducible with random splitting). Worth testing if stratified splitting is feasible.

Compare variance to random splitting for per-category metrics

hypotheses.title: External Gene-Disease Database Integration: DisGeNET/OMIM for Mechanism Coverage Expansion
hypotheses.rationale: h719+h722 confirm DRKG gene-gene 2-hop is too dense for mechanism specificity. But 77.8% of would-be-MEDIUM predictions lack 1-hop mechanism because DRKG's disease-gene annotations are incomplete (139 diseases have 0 genes). DisGeNET and OMIM contain much richer gene-disease associations. Supplementing DRKG with external gene-disease data could expand 1-hop mechanism coverage without the 2-hop specificity problem. This is the remaining path to expanding MEDIUM tier beyond current rules.
steps: Download DisGeNET gene-disease associations (free academic license)
Map DisGeNET disease IDs to DRKG MESH IDs
Count how many of the 139 gene-poor diseases gain genes from DisGeNET
Re-evaluate mechanism coverage on holdout
If coverage expands >20%, implement as supplementary gene source

hypotheses.title: Hierarchy Rule Consolidation: Merge Small Groups Into Parent Categories
hypotheses.description:
h760 found 10 holdout-invisible rules and 1 dead rule. Many hierarchy groups 
have only 1-2 GT diseases, making individual evaluation impossible. Consider merging small groups 
into their parent category (e.g., all autoimmune hierarchy groups → single autoimmune_hierarchy rule). 
This would increase n/seed for holdout evaluation while maintaining the category-level signal. 
Trade-off: lose within-category discrimination (e.g., psoriasis vs lupus vs MS) but gain evaluability.
steps: For each category, compute merged holdout precision across all hierarchy sub-groups
Compare merged vs individual rule performance for evaluable rules
If merged precision is similar, simplify by removing sub-group discrimination
If individual rules perform differently, keep separate where evaluable

hypotheses.title: 15-Seed Holdout Evaluation: Reduce Never-Holdout Diseases from 33% to 3.5%
hypotheses.description: h770 found 337 diseases (32.6%) never appear in 5-seed holdout, causing +7.8pp GOLDEN and +8.2pp MEDIUM inflation. Using 15 seeds would reduce never-holdout to ~36 diseases (3.5%). This gives more accurate precision estimates without changing the tier system. Main cost: 3x longer evaluation runs.
steps: Modify h393 evaluator to support configurable seed count (default 5)
Run 15-seed evaluation and compare tier precisions to 5-seed
If precisions change significantly (>3pp), update all reference precision values
Assess runtime cost vs precision improvement tradeoff

hypotheses.title: GOLDEN Calibration: Adjust Full-Data GOLDEN Precision Reporting from 92% to 88%
hypotheses.description: h770 showed GOLDEN full-data precision (92.2%) is inflated by +7.8pp due to 53.9% of predictions coming from never-holdout diseases. The visible-only precision (88.0%) is closer to true holdout. Consider whether GOLDEN precision constants should use visible-only estimates for more honest calibration.
steps: Compare h770 visible-only precision to actual 5-seed holdout precision for each tier
If visible-only is within 3pp of holdout, adopt visible-only as calibration reference
Update precision constants in production_predictor.py if warranted

hypotheses.title: Per-Disease Holdout Coverage: Annotate Predictions with Holdout Evaluation Confidence
hypotheses.description: h770 found diseases with 0 holdout appearances have +8pp higher precision than diseases seen in holdout. Annotating each prediction with how often its disease appears in holdout (0-5 seeds) would help users understand which precision estimates are more vs less reliable. Diseases seen in 3+ seeds have the most reliable precision estimates.
steps: Add holdout_appearances (0-5) to each disease in deliverable
Flag diseases with 0 appearances as holdout_invisible
Include visible-only precision as alternative calibration for these diseases

Compare rescue rates to PubMed

Identify common patterns that could benefit from new simplification rules

Can we further reduce variance by: (1) identifying and demoting high-variance GOLDEN rules, or (2) promoting more low-variance HIGH rules? Target: ± 2.0% or lower for maximum deliverable confidence.

Mining these provides: (1) validation that hierarchy rules have literature support, (2) GT gap detection for FDA-approved uses, (3) safety catch for any misclassified predictions. Low effort, medium impact.

Run literature mining (PubMed + ClinicalTrials.gov) on each
Identify GT gaps (STRONG evidence but not in expanded GT)
Flag any non-STRONG predictions for safety review

hypotheses.title: Validate 159 Uncached Inverse Indication FILTER Predictions via Literature Mining
hypotheses.description: h800 found 159 inverse_indication FILTER predictions without literature cache. All 9 cached inverse_indication entries had 100% STRONG evidence (confirming drug CAUSES disease). Mining these validates the safety filter and may find FALSE inverse_indications where the drug actually treats the condition. Each false positive removed = prediction rescued from FILTER.

Run literature mining on each
Identify any pairs where evidence supports TREATMENT not HARM
Remove false inverse_indication entries
Re-run holdout evaluation

hypotheses.title: Literature-Free LOW Tier Rescue: Can Drug/Disease Features Identify Hidden HIGH-Quality Predictions?
hypotheses.description: h800 showed mining LOW/FILTER broadly is futile (0% STRONG in 1,056 cached LOW). But 8,675 LOW predictions at 11.6% holdout means ~1,006 ARE correct. Instead of literature mining, can drug/disease-level features identify which LOW predictions are high-quality? Features to test: (1) disease GT richness (GT count), (2) drug therapeutic breadth (number of indications), (3) kNN neighborhood quality (mean neighbor GT overlap), (4) TransE rank. If a feature subset achieves >30% holdout, those LOW predictions could be promoted to MEDIUM.
steps: For all LOW predictions, compute: GT count of disease, GT count of drug, TransE rank, neighbor overlap
Run holdout evaluation stratified by each feature
Identify any feature threshold achieving >30% holdout
If found, implement as LOW→MEDIUM promotion rule
Validate on 5-seed holdout
hypotheses.findings: Analysis found several LOW subsets with MEDIUM-quality holdout: (1) rich_disease(GT≥30)+high_score(≥3): 37.8% ± 6.9% (n=78/seed), non-CS 32.5% — borderline MEDIUM but would rescue predictions from correctly-calibrated demotion rules (antimicrobial_pathogen_mismatch, neurological_medium_demotion, etc.). (2) score≥5: 59.8% ± 6.1% (n=13/seed) — too small and 67% CS. (3) default_freq10_nomech_r6_10 sub-reason: 32.1% (n=52/seed) but already demoted from MEDIUM. (4) TransE+score≥3: 37.1% (n=21/seed), 62% CS. Key insight: disease GT richness (24.0% for GT≥50 vs 3.0% for GT≤4) and kNN score are strongest LOW-internal signals, but promoting broadly would undo safety demotions. No clean, safe promotion rule identified.
hypotheses.result_metric: INCONCLUSIVE: Best LOW subset 37.8% (rich+high_score) but unsafe to promote broadly

hypotheses.title: MODERATE_EVIDENCE Literature Level: Integrate 550 Unhandled Cache Entries
hypotheses.description: h805 discovered that MODERATE_EVIDENCE (550 entries in literature_mining_cache.json) is not handled by production_predictor.py. These predictions are treated as NOT_ASSESSED, meaning they bypass all literature-based tier modifications (h789 promotion, h791 demotion, h732 demotion, h795 promotion). Need to evaluate MODERATE_EVIDENCE holdout precision across tiers: (1) Should MODERATE + HIGH → stay HIGH or demote to MEDIUM? (2) Should MODERATE + MEDIUM → stay MEDIUM or promote/demote? (3) Should MODERATE + LOW/FILTER → promote to HIGH like STRONG?
steps: Run holdout evaluation for predictions with MODERATE_EVIDENCE across all current tiers
Compare MODERATE to WEAK and STRONG boundaries
If MODERATE+HIGH >= 55%: leave as HIGH (no demotion needed)
If MODERATE+LOW >= 55%: promote like STRONG
Implement appropriate tier modifications
hypotheses.findings:
LOW + MODERATE_EVIDENCE analysis:
- All: 33.2% ± 5.4% (n=37/seed, 185 total) — near MEDIUM (34.8%) but includes 'other' drag
- Non-other: 40.2% ± 12.9% (n=24/seed) — above MEDIUM avg but HIGH variance
- Non-other non-CS: 36.6% ± 11.4% (n=21/seed) — marginal
- Per-seed range: 20.8% to 57.1% (too unstable)
- No safety-demoted predictions (all are genuinely LOW)
- 'other' category = 21.9% (h798 pattern confirmed)
- Category breakdown: musculoskeletal 55.6%, autoimmune 55.6%, ophthalmic 75.0%, infectious 37.3%, dermatological 11.1%
CONCLUSION: Signal exists but n<30 and variance too high (±12.9%). Not reliable enough for LOW→MEDIUM promotion.
HIGH+MODERATE (63.2%) and MEDIUM+MODERATE (40.6%) correctly placed — no action needed.
hypotheses.result_metric: LOW+MODERATE non-other: 40.2% ± 12.9% (too high variance, n=24/seed)

hypotheses.title: Literature Evidence Coverage Expansion: Mine Remaining Un-cached HIGH/MEDIUM Predictions
hypotheses.description: h808 showed that literature evidence quality varies dramatically by sub-reason. Currently only ~590 predictions are in the literature mining cache. Many HIGH and MEDIUM predictions have NOT_ASSESSED literature status and bypass the demotion/promotion rules entirely. Add FILTER rule with mechanism-gate escape (anti-inflammatory antibiotic exceptions list)
Confirm ≤1.5σ MEDIUM/LOW precision shift after demotion; report preds-filtered count

hypotheses.title: Backwards-search for other never-fired branches in production_predictor
hypotheses.description: The h900 fallback was dead code from day one because self.train_diseases is pre-filtered to require GT + embeddings — an invariant the fallback author missed. Other branches in production_predictor.py may be similarly unreachable: rescue paths gated on conditions that the upstream tier assignment already eliminates, safety-filter early-exits inside else-blocks the safety filter never reaches, etc. A coverage-style trace would surface them cheaply.

Run h393 5-seed holdout under coverage; aggregate per-line hit counts
Surface every branch with hit_count == 0 across all 5 seeds
For each, classify: (a) genuinely unreachable (remove), (b) reachable but underused (consider rule weakening), (c) reachable on data we don't see in 80% sample (mark with comment)
Report number of removed lines and any tier-precision delta after cleanup

hypotheses.title: Why does kNN ALWAYS populate drug_scores when disease_id has an embedding?
hypotheses.description: h903 reported drug_scores is always populated when disease_id is in self.embeddings. The cause (per CLAUDE.md) is that self.train_diseases is pre-filtered to require both GT entries and embeddings. But this only guarantees train neighbors *exist*, not that any of their GT drugs survive the `if drug_id in self.embeddings` check at line 4660. A formal proof would let us delete the `if not drug_scores:` guard entirely and shrink predict() further. Worth checking whether neighbor GT drugs without embeddings get silently dropped 100% of the time on some disease.
steps: Instrument the inner loop at production_predictor.py:4659 to count, per neighbor, how many GT drugs lack embeddings vs how many survive
Run on full 1034-disease evaluable set; emit max/min surviving-drug count
If min > 0, the if-guard can be removed entirely (replace with assert + comment)
If min == 0 for some disease, document the failure mode and keep the guard

hypotheses.title: Cancer-Gene-Signature De-biasing for Target-Overlap Scoring
hypotheses.rationale: h916 showed cancer's high target_r30 comes from a shared cancer-gene vocabulary (oncogenes, kinases, TSGs, cell-cycle) inflating overlap mechanically. If we subtract the cancer-cross-disease shared-gene signature from both drug-target and disease-gene sets, does the residual target-overlap score distinguish TRUE cancer repurposing vs pan-cancer non-specific? Positive control: pembrolizumab→melanoma should retain signal; negative control: generic kinase inhibitor should lose most signal.
steps: Compute cancer-gene-signature: genes present in >=50% of cancer disease gene-sets (n=104)
Compute drug-cancer-signature: genes present in >=50% of cancer drugs' target sets
Re-score target-overlap with shared-signature genes removed from both sides
Compare ranks of known cancer drug-disease pairs pre- vs post-debiasing
Report whether debiased target_r30 still concentrates in cancer

hypotheses.title: Does max_overlap magnitude outperform target_r30 as a ranking signal?
hypotheses.rationale: h916 found target_r30 is near-zero for non-cancer categories despite reasonable max_overlap counts (e.g., autoimmune 10.5, renal 9.6, psychiatric 8.2). The target ranker currently uses overlap as feature but R@30 hit rate is low because it lacks scale awareness. Test whether log(max_overlap)*Jaccard(drug_targets, disease_genes) beats raw overlap for these categories. Low effort: per-disease re-rank using h912 records and existing drug_targets.json.
steps: For each non-cancer category (n>=20 diseases), re-rank candidate drugs with Jaccard
Compare R@30 per disease vs raw max_overlap ranking from h912
If Jaccard improves R@30 by >=2pp in any category, flag that category for h906 priority
Save per-category delta to data/analysis/h938_jaccard_vs_raw.json

hypotheses.title: Cancer Target-Overlap as Subtype Discriminator Within-Cancer
hypotheses.rationale: h916 showed cancer drugs have high overlap with cancer-disease gene-sets generally. But within-cancer, does target-overlap discriminate the RIGHT subtype (e.g., EGFR mutant NSCLC vs KRAS mutant NSCLC)? h730 found targeted therapy is ~6% holdout with high full-data inflation — biomarker profiles aren't in embeddings. Test: for 20 cancer diseases with biomarker-segregated GT drugs, does target-overlap rank the matched-biomarker drug higher than the unmatched drug?
steps: Curate 20 cancer subtype diseases with known biomarker-specific GT drugs
For each, compute target-overlap rank of matched-biomarker drug vs all-cancer drug pool
Compute median rank and AUROC for matched vs unmatched within cancer
If median rank <=30, target-overlap is a subtype discriminator; if >100, it is not

hypotheses.title: Biologic Flag Refinement: DrugBank Biotech Category vs USAN-Suffix Proxy
hypotheses.rationale: h939 used a USAN-suffix + keyword proxy (266 drugs) for the biologic flag. If the h939 signal is partly driven by naming-convention artifacts (peptide -tide drugs that are really small molecules; enzymes that are not biologics in the mAb/fusion-protein sense), the 3x ratio could weaken. Cross-check with DrugBank's biotech vs small-molecule classification. Low priority because h939 ratios are 3-11x - unlikely to flip the decision.
steps: Register for DrugBank academic license (if not already)
Extract drug 'type' field for each DrugBank ID in drug_targets
Compute overlap and disagreement with USAN-suffix proxy
Re-run h939 analysis restricted to DrugBank-confirmed biotech drugs
Compare per-category ratios; report whether conclusions hold

hypotheses.title: Why Does Target-Overlap Fail for Small Molecules? Polypharmacy Dilution Test
hypotheses.rationale: h939 showed small-molecule target_r30 is only 5.5% vs biologic 26.5%. Hypothesis: small molecules have many targets (polypharmacy), so off-target overlap with disease gene sets dilutes the signal. If true, restricting SM target-overlap to drugs with <=3 targets should narrow the gap. A 'specificity-weighted target-overlap' score could extend the h906 benefit to selective small molecules (kinase inhibitors, GPCR-selective agents).
steps: From h939 records compute mean n_targets for biologic pool vs SM pool
Re-run SM target-overlap restricted to drugs with <=3 targets
Compare sm_r30_specific vs sm_r30_all and against biologic baseline
If specificity-restricted SM approaches biologic levels, consider specificity weighting in h940

hypotheses.title: Inverse Problem: Biologic Zero-Overlap as Confidence Signal for 'Unlikely Indication'
hypotheses.rationale: h939 showed biologic target-overlap is a strong POSITIVE signal. The inverse: when a biologic is predicted by kNN but has ZERO target overlap with the disease gene set, how often is this a false positive? Biologics are mechanism-specific, so zero-overlap should be a strong negative predictor for biologics. If validated, this becomes an inverse-indication filter - exactly the kind of precision pivot called out in research_spec.md Section 5 (Inverse Problems).
steps: Partition current MEDIUM/HIGH biologic predictions into (a) target-overlap>0 and (b) target-overlap=0
Compute holdout precision for each subset across 5 seeds
If (b) precision <= 10% AND (a) precision >= 25%, add biologic zero-overlap -> FILTER rule
Sanity-check that the filter does not remove known-correct predictions

hypotheses.title: Biologic Coverage Stratification: Does kNN-only bio_r30 mask rare-biologic failures?
hypotheses.rationale: h940 showed pure kNN gives biologic R@30=31.4% baseline — higher than the 27.3% quoted. Hypothesis: this average hides bimodal behavior. Common biologics (adalimumab, rituximab, bevacizumab, infliximab) appear in many neighbor GT and inflate the mean, while rare/orphan biologics (enzyme replacements, gene-therapy vectors, rare-disease mAbs) still fail silently. If the bottom 50% of biologics by train-frequency have R@30<<top 50%, the 'biologic failure' bucket reappears under a different name.
steps: Reuse h940 holdout runs. For each holdout disease and biologic GT drug, record rank (or miss) in the baseline kNN top-N (N=100) and the biologic's train_freq.
Stratify bio_r30 by biologic train_freq quartile (Q1 = most common, Q4 = rarest).
Compute bio_r30 per quartile; bootstrap 95% CI.
If Q4 bio_r30 << 10%, rare biologics ARE the failure class — not all biologics.
Report how many Q4 biologics would be recovered if target-overlap alone were the tiebreaker for ties at rank 30.

hypotheses.title: Biologic Zero-Overlap Safety Filter: demote biologic predictions with zero disease-gene overlap
hypotheses.rationale: Inverting h940's failure: if fusion HURT recall, the overlap signal may still work as a NEGATIVE filter. A biologic predicted for a disease whose gene set shares ZERO targets with the drug is likely a kNN co-prescription artifact (procedural/adjunct, not mechanism-of-action). Unlike small molecules (polypharmacy, indirect mechanisms), biologic efficacy almost always requires target engagement. Test: for biologic preds in MEDIUM/LOW tier with zero target-overlap, is holdout precision materially lower than the tier average?
steps: From production deliverable, partition MEDIUM and LOW biologic predictions into zero-overlap vs >=1-overlap.
Compute 5-seed holdout precision per subset.
If zero-overlap biologic precision is >1.5σ below cohort average, add biologic_zero_overlap FILTER tier rule.
Validate no golden/high biologic predictions are incidentally demoted.

hypotheses.title: Biologic Fusion-as-Annotation: use fused score only as meta-confidence feature
hypotheses.rationale: h940's alpha=0.9 fusion lifted bio_p30 from 17.58% to 21.32% (+3.74pp) — a precision win — while hurting recall. If the fusion ranking is used ONLY to annotate predictions (not to re-rank), the meta-confidence model can learn when agreement between kNN and target-overlap correlates with holdout hit. Non-destructive; doesn't change the main ranking; adds a feature.
steps: For each prediction in the deliverable that is a biologic, compute target_overlap_norm and kNN_norm.
Define biologic_fusion_agreement = min(target_overlap_norm, kNN_norm) — rewards both signals.
Train / re-fit confidence calibrator with this feature added.
Measure holdout precision uplift at biologic predictions only; check tier-shift regressions.

hypotheses.title: Biologic precision pivot — exploit bio_p30 = 6.37% with biologic-aware tier promotion
hypotheses.rationale: h951 found bio_r30 = 27.06% (recall is fine) but bio_p30 = 6.37% (precision is poor — fewer than 2 of 30 top-30 predictions are biologics that hit GT). For diseases with no biologic GT, ANY biologic in top-30 is a precision drag. For diseases with biologic GT, the biologic predictions are sparse and often wrong. Test: for each disease, compute a 'biologic-likelihood' prior from disease features (immunological category, ATC L code, treatment class history) and DEMOTE biologic predictions in top-30 for diseases with low biologic prior. Should improve overall precision without hurting overall recall.
steps: Compute per-disease biologic-prior: P(disease has >=1 biologic GT) from train-only categorical features (category, has_immunology_keywords, has_targeted_therapy_keywords).
On holdout, simulate demoting biologic predictions to FILTER for diseases with biologic_prior < 0.1.
Measure overall precision@30, bio precision, bio recall on holdout.
Decision: if overall precision improves >=2pp without bio_r30 dropping >5pp, ship as a tier rule.
hypotheses.findings: INVALIDATED. 5-seed h393 holdout, top_n=200, thresholds {0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20,0.30}. Baseline p30=14.32%±0.94%, r30=19.79%±1.59%, bio_r30=30.31%±3.57% (avg 3.4 biologics in top-30). Best p30 lift = +0.05pp (thr=0.30) — far below the +2pp ship gate. At thr=0.10 only infectious (prior=0.088) qualifies for demotion (~24 dx/seed) and is precision-neutral (per-category p30 Δ=0.00pp everywhere; bio_r30 -0.18pp). At thr=0.15+ demotion expands to other, psychiatric, dermatological — costs bio_r30 -5.6 to -8.2pp without moving p30. Mechanism (3 reasons): (1) baseline kNN already concentrates biologics in immunology/cancer-class diseases — few are misplaced; (2) the rank-31+ non-biologic replacement hits at the same background rate as the demoted biologic, so the swap is precision-neutral; (3) category-level prior is too coarse — dermatological has prior=0.183 but bio_r30=72.2% (real biologic hits would be lost). The hypothesis premise that low-prior-category biologics are a precision drag is FALSE. Filed h990 (kNN-neighbor-derived per-disease prior, finer-grained) and h991 (category-prior-aware promotion for high-prior categories with target-overlap, inverse direction).
hypotheses.result_metric: p30 Δ=+0.05pp (max), bio_r30 Δ=-8.16pp (worst); ship gate (+2pp p30, ≤5pp bio_r30 drop) NOT met at any threshold

hypotheses.title: Re-evaluate GB-enhanced model on production eval framework to enable apples-to-apples comparison
hypotheses.rationale: h954 established that the GB-enhanced 41.8% is micro-averaged per-drug pair recall on a smaller Every-Cure-only GT, while production h951/h958 is macro-averaged per-disease R@30 on expanded GT. To know whether GB is actually better or worse than kNN+tier production, we'd need to run GB through the same eval framework: 5-seed 80/20 disease holdout, per-disease R@30, expanded GT. This is a meta-science question — not expected to change the production pipeline, but would tell us if we're leaving per-drug-pair signal on the table. If GB scores ≥20% per-disease R@30 under production eval, could justify a hybrid.
steps: Write scripts/h966_gb_enhanced_production_eval.py reusing h393_holdout_tier_validation.py eval harness.
Replace predictor.predict() with GB model scoring drug×disease pair features.
Rank top-30 drugs per holdout disease; compute per-disease R@30 mean across 5 seeds.
Compare to h958 19.49%; decide whether to pursue GB+kNN hybrid.
hypotheses.success_criteria: Per-disease R@30 comparison to h958 within same eval framework; no commitment to action unless GB ≥ 20%.

hypotheses.title: Document the micro-vs-macro R@30 pitfall in CLAUDE.md as a scientific-methodology entry
hypotheses.rationale: h954 found that 'baseline drift' was actually an eval-framework mismatch (micro-pool per-drug vs macro per-disease on different GT). Without a named rule, future agents are likely to confuse any R@30 quote. Add a short 'metric hygiene' note to CLAUDE.md: when quoting R@30, always specify (a) macro-per-disease vs micro-per-drug-pair, (b) GT version (EC-only vs expanded), (c) eval split (static vs n-seed holdout), (d) model path (GB classifier vs kNN+tier). This prevents recurrence of the h954 confusion.
steps: Add a 'Metric Hygiene' subsection under 'Key Metrics' in CLAUDE.md.
List the four disambiguation axes and the current production default (macro per-disease, expanded GT, 5-seed 80/20, production_predictor.predict()).
Reference h954 for the full reconciliation.
hypotheses.success_criteria: CLAUDE.md section added; future validated hypotheses include all four axes when quoting R@30.

hypotheses.title: Per-prediction biologic-low-mechanism-evidence ANNOTATION (not tier demotion)
hypotheses.rationale: h957/h965 confirmed target-overlap is a real biologic precision signal in oncology (+2.5pp p30) but too narrow to ship as a global tier rule (h965 global delta = +0.28pp). Instead of demoting predictions, expose the signal as a deliverable column: `biologic_low_mechanism_evidence` = True when (is_biologic AND drug_targets non-empty AND disease_genes non-empty AND overlap == 0). Users / downstream consumers (Ryland review, EveryCure evaluators) can filter by this flag without globally moving tier metrics. Validates the precision finding without paying the global recall cost. Especially valuable for the 47 GOLDEN/HIGH zero-overlap biologic preds (h967 audit candidates) — annotate them clearly so reviewers know to double-check the evidence before treating them as high-confidence.
steps: Add a column `biologic_low_mechanism_evidence` (True/False) to scripts/generate_production_deliverable.py output.
Set True iff is_biologic(drug) AND drug_targets[d] non-empty AND disease_genes[D] non-empty AND |drug_targets[d] ∩ disease_genes[D]| == 0.
Cross-check counts vs h957 dropped_tier_counts (expect ~3,936 True flags in deliverable, mostly in LOW/FILTER).
Coordinate with h962 deliverable regeneration so h957/h968 ship together.

hypotheses.title: Cancer biologic subclass-restricted overlap filter (anti-HER2, anti-VEGF, checkpoint, anti-CD20)
hypotheses.rationale: h957/h965 found the zero-overlap signal works cleanly in oncology because cancer disease_genes are TCGA-dense and biologic MoA in oncology is target-driven. But h957's 2.74x bio:sm ratio in cancer (h939) is the weakest of the four 'biologics-dominate' categories — h916 traced this to the shared cancer-gene vocabulary. The subset where target-overlap should be MOST diagnostic is cancer biologics with very specific, well-characterized single-target MoA: anti-HER2 (trastuzumab, pertuzumab, T-DM1), anti-VEGF (bevacizumab, ramucirumab), anti-CD20 (rituximab, obinutuzumab, ofatumumab), checkpoint inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab, atezolizumab, durvalumab). If we restrict the filter to these ~20 drugs in cancer-category diseases, expected effect is: very small drop count (~10-20/seed vs h965's 70-90), but very high signal-to-noise per drop. Test if precision lift WITHIN this subclass is +5pp+ at <2pp recall cost.
steps: Curate canonical drug list (~20-30 drug_ids) for the four MoA subclasses.
Modify h965 filter to fire only when (drug in subclass AND category=='cancer').
Run 5-seed h393 holdout, report subclass-cohort and global deltas.
Decision: ship if subclass-cohort delta_bio_p30 >= +5pp at delta_bio_r30 >= -2pp (relaxed because n is small and signal-to-noise should be high).

hypotheses.title: SELECTIVE_BOOST ablation on neurological — find the real h952 regression source
hypotheses.rationale: h960 ruled out the h173 supplement as the cause of the h952 -2.85pp boost+supp neurological regression. h952 boost_only stratum showed +1.41pp (boost helps on metabolic/renal/hematological/respiratory/immunological). The combined boost+supp neurological -2.85pp must therefore come from SELECTIVE_BOOST behaving differently on neurological than on the other SELECTIVE_BOOST_CATEGORIES. Test: ablate boost for neurological category specifically (i.e., remove 'neurological' from SELECTIVE_BOOST_CATEGORIES), re-run 5-seed holdout, measure neuro overall_r30 delta vs current production.
steps: Monkey-patch SELECTIVE_BOOST_CATEGORIES to exclude 'neurological'.
Run 5-seed h393 holdout. Measure neuro_overall_r30 baseline vs ablated.
Non-neuro control should be 0pp.
Decision: if neuro_overall_r30 lifts >=+1.5pp without hurting non-neuro, propose removing 'neurological' from SELECTIVE_BOOST_CATEGORIES.

hypotheses.title: Per-disease predict() vs plain-kNN top-30 set-diff localization on neurological holdout
hypotheses.rationale: h960 + h972 narrow the search but do not pinpoint *which* drugs are being swapped in/out of the top-30 by SELECTIVE_BOOST on neuro diseases. For each holdout neuro disease (n≈13/seed in the boost+supp stratum), produce a side-by-side table: top-30 plain-kNN drugs, top-30 predict() drugs, the set difference (added/removed), and which side intersects the GT. This directly explains the -2.85pp by drug name. Likely pattern: boost amplifies neighbor diseases that share neuro-irrelevant drugs (e.g., common anti-epileptics for an unrelated movement disorder), displacing the neighbor-disease drugs that ARE GT-correct.
steps: For each holdout neuro disease at seed 42, dump plain-kNN top-30 vs predict() top-30, expanded GT, and highlight added/removed drugs.
Categorize the swaps by drug class (anti-epileptic, dopaminergic, anti-inflammatory, etc.) to identify systematic boost-induced false positives.
Output one CSV per disease (n≈13) for manual review.

hypotheses.title: GOLDEN std 4.6x widening — decompose seed-42 / seed-789 dip
hypotheses.rationale: h964 found GOLDEN std widened from 1.3→6.0 (4.6x) post-h952-fix, driven by seeds 42 and 789 dropping to 71-72% while seeds 123/456/2024 stayed ≥78%. This indicates disease-split-dependent GOLDEN hits: specific newly-resolving diseases (previously silent-zero) contribute GOLDEN misses only when they land in the holdout. Identifying which categories or specific diseases cause these dips tells us whether the wider CI is (a) a few bad apples in newly-resolved names, (b) systematic for a category, or (c) random sampling noise. Low-effort: re-read h393 holdout JSON + intersect with disease_names that needed the h952 reverse-index fallback.
steps: Build a list of 287 names that required the h952 reverse-index fallback (from h959 audit).
For seeds 42 and 789, extract the holdout diseases that came ONLY from that set — i.e., diseases silent-zeroed pre-fix.
For those diseases, count per-disease GOLDEN tier preds and hit rate.
Compare to always-resolved diseases in the same seeds. Is GOLDEN-miss concentration above baseline?
If yes, name the category or rule; if no, classify as random seed noise.
hypotheses.success_criteria: Either identify a systematic pattern (category, rule, or disease-class) OR show the variance is random. Update CLAUDE.md h964 entry with the root cause.

hypotheses.title: 10-seed h393 GOLDEN/HIGH boundary reality check
hypotheses.rationale: h964 post-fix saw GOLDEN (78.5 ± 6.0) fall below HIGH (80.0 ± 3.3) at mean, but CIs overlap (72.5–84.5 vs 76.7–83.3). A tier inversion at the top of the system is a headline finding if real. Running 10 seeds (vs 5) halves the std and resolves whether the inversion is a robust structural feature or seed noise. Cost is ~2x current h393 runtime (~10 min).
steps: Parameterize h393 script to accept --seeds; run with 10 seeds.
Compare 10-seed GOLDEN vs HIGH means + tightened CIs.
If inversion persists at 10 seeds with non-overlapping CIs, file h-follow-up to re-examine GOLDEN rule set.
If inversion disappears, close the thread — it was noise.
hypotheses.success_criteria: Binary: inversion is real (GOLDEN < HIGH after tightening CIs) vs noise. Resolves the h964 tier-ordering ambiguity.

hypotheses.title: Demote immunological_medium_demotion LOW→FILTER on post-fix evidence
hypotheses.rationale: h975 found immunological_medium_demotion holdout precision dropped from 8.3%→2.6% at n=23/seed (115 across 5 seeds), now 7.4pp below the LOW tier mean of 10.0%. The rule was demoted from MEDIUM to LOW by h462/h553 but post-fix data suggests it should drop one more tier. Simple tier reassignment.
steps: Locate immunological_medium_demotion assignment in production_predictor.py tier-rule block.
Change LOW → FILTER.
Run h393 5-seed; confirm LOW tier precision does not drop and FILTER tier precision does not spike.
Net impact: +0.08pp LOW precision (remove 23 preds at 2.6% hit rate); net 0 on FILTER.
hypotheses.success_criteria: LOW tier precision stable or slightly improved; no regressions.

hypotheses.title: Audit all predict(name) call sites for disease_id-in-name-string bug
steps: grep all '.predict(' call sites across scripts/ and src/.
For each, check whether the first arg could be a disease_id (drkg: prefix) or only a name.
Flag mismatches; migrate disease_id callers to use the h963 fast-path.

hypotheses.title: Add a public predict_by_id() method as the preferred production interface
steps: Introduce `DrugRepurposingPredictor.predict_by_id(disease_id, ...)` as a thin wrapper that validates disease_id in embeddings and calls the internal fast-path.
Keep predict(disease_name) for the user-facing name path.

hypotheses.title: h771 drug_disease_groups leak — script restores at end but never recomputes during holdout

hypotheses.title: Over-demotion audit: MEDIUM→LOW (lit_weak) at 19.1% sits 4.3pp above LOW average
hypotheses.hypothesis: If the weak-literature demotion is too aggressive, the demoted subset would score closer to MEDIUM than LOW. h771 post-h963 shows 19.1% — partially calibrated. Inspect whether the 53 demoted preds/seed include any that should have stayed MEDIUM.

Compare hit rate for the top-quartile of demoted preds vs bottom-quartile.
If top quartile scores near MEDIUM (40%+), adjust the rule to require STRICT weak criteria (zero PubMed hits + no trials) rather than mere ABSENCE of strong evidence.
Rerun h771 and h393 to measure tier impact.

hypotheses.title: MEDIUM(lit=NOT_ASSESSED) at 46.2% exceeds MEDIUM avg — literature cache has coverage gap, not a signal
hypotheses.hypothesis: NOT_ASSESSED means the literature miner didn't look at this drug-disease pair. Their above-average 46.2% precision means NOT_ASSESSED is not a quality signal — it's just a coverage gap. Verify by running literature mining on the NOT_ASSESSED bucket and checking whether scoring changes.

Re-evaluate with newly-scored predictions and measure MEDIUM(lit=*) breakdown.

hypotheses.title: Measure h961 downstream impact on h393 5-seed tier precisions
hypotheses.description: h961 added 776 new mesh_mappings entries and moved the 668 disease_names entries from the h952 runtime fallback to direct mm resolution. Does this affect any downstream eval? Run h393 5-seed post-h961, diff vs h964 post-fix, report tier-precision deltas. If deltas >1pp on any tier, investigate and decide whether to surface the change in the deliverable row count.
steps: Run scripts/h393_holdout_tier_validation.py 5 seeds post-h961.
Diff tier precisions vs h964 baseline (GOLDEN 78.5%, HIGH 80.0%, MEDIUM 39.9%, LOW 10.0%, FILTER 6.8%).
If any |Δ|>1pp, trace to newly-resolvable diseases added by h961.
Re-generate the 13,416-row deliverable and diff row count.

hypotheses.title: Retire h952 runtime fallback once h961 canonicalization covers all disease_names
hypotheses.description: h952 added a reverse-index fallback in find_disease_id for 668 disease_names missing from mesh_mappings. h961 now populates those 668 directly into mesh_mappings at load time, so the fallback is dead code for the original failure cases. BUT the fallback may still fire for out-of-band canonical names not in the h961 alias file. Approach: instrument find_disease_id for 1k production calls to measure fallback hit-rate post-h961. If hit-rate ≈0, retire the fallback; if it still fires, regenerate h961 aliases and re-ship. Includes a small CI regression test asserting the disease_names backfill coverage.

hypotheses.title: Per-disease kNN-neighbor biologic prior (finer-grained than h953)
hypotheses.rationale: h953 invalidated per-CATEGORY prior demotion because categories are too coarse (dermatological prior=0.18 but bio_r30=72%). Test the same idea with a PER-DISEASE prior computed as the fraction of that disease's top-k kNN neighbors (in train) that have ≥1 biologic in their expanded GT. This aligns the prior with the actual mechanism kNN uses to score biologics, and should isolate diseases where zero neighbors support biologics (strong demotion candidates) from diseases where biologics ARE in the neighbor set but happen to be in a low-prior category.
steps: For each holdout disease, find its top-20 kNN neighbors in train (same as production predict()).
prior(d) = (#neighbors with ≥1 biologic in expanded GT) / 20.
Sweep thresholds in {0.0 (strict: zero neighbors), 0.05, 0.10, 0.20}. Demote biologics to FILTER for diseases with prior below threshold; refill top-30 from next non-biologics.
Measure overall p30/r30/bio_r30 across 5 seeds vs h958 baseline.
Decision: ship if p30 ≥ +2pp and bio_r30 drop ≤ 3pp; otherwise document as bounded-ceiling for biologic precision via kNN-derived signals.
hypotheses.findings: INVALIDATED. 5-seed h393 holdout, top_n=200, k=20, thresholds {0.00,0.05,0.10,0.20}. Baseline p30=14.32%±0.94%, r30=19.79%±1.59%, bio_r30=30.31%±3.57%. Best p30 lift = +0.01pp (thr=0.20) — far below the +1pp ship gate. **Strict thr=0.00 (zero top-20 neighbors with any biologic in expanded GT): 19 dx demoted/seed but bio_r30 Δ=+0.00pp** — proving that for these 19 diseases per seed, ZERO biologics were in baseline top-30. This is the kNN structural invariant: drug_scores only sums over neighbor GT, so zero biologic neighbors -> zero biologics in any top-N. At thr=0.10 (43 demoted/seed), bio_r30 -1.37pp with no p30 movement. At thr=0.20 (99 demoted/seed), bio_r30 -6.94pp with p30 +0.01pp. **Deeper insight than h953:** even with the FINEST-grained per-disease prior we can construct, the conclusion holds — removing in-top-30 biologics costs bio_r30, replacements from rank 31+ hit at the same background rate, p30 stays flat. The rank 31-200 tail is a uniform-quality bucket with no exploitable signal differentiation. Filed h993 (per-rank hit-rate audit to formalize the tail-uniformity claim) and h994 (precision pivot must operate INSIDE rank 1-30 via re-ranking, not in-out shuffle). Raw: data/analysis/h990_neighbor_bio_prior.json, data/analysis/h990_run.txt.
hypotheses.result_metric: p30 Δ=+0.01pp (max), bio_r30 Δ=-6.94pp (worst); strict thr=0.00 confirmed kNN structural invariant (zero biologic neighbors -> zero biologics in top-30)

hypotheses.title: Inverse of h953 — small-molecule precision gap is the real pivot (bio_r30=30% > overall_r30=20%)
hypotheses.rationale: h953 baseline measurement confirms bio_r30=30.31% > overall_r30=19.79% — a +10.5pp gap in the OPPOSITE direction of the h906/h920/h921/h924 'biologic failure' narrative (already dissolved in h951). This means precision lift must come from SMALL-MOLECULE slots, not biologic slots. Test: stratify the 14.32% baseline p30 by small-molecule vs biologic rank-position. Compute sm_p30 (precision among small-molecule top-30 entries). Compare sm_p30 to bio_p30 per disease category. Any category where sm_p30 < bio_p30 is a candidate for a small-molecule demote.
steps: Reuse h953 per-disease records (data/analysis/h953_biologic_precision_pivot.json lacks SM split; rerun with explicit sm_p30 collection).
For each category, compute mean sm_p30, mean bio_p30. Identify categories where sm_p30 is ≥5pp below bio_p30.
For those categories, propose a targeted SM demote rule (e.g. drop SM predictions whose rank is low AND whose train_frequency < 3, filling with next best).
Measure on 5-seed holdout: if overall p30 improves ≥1pp without r30 dropping ≥2pp, ship.
hypotheses.findings: INVALIDATED — hypothesis framing was backwards. 5-seed h393 holdout pooled: sm_p30|sm = 15.48%, bio_p30|bio = 5.64%. Gap is −9.85pp meaning SM OUTPERFORMS bio slot-for-slot, not the reverse. bio_r30 > overall_r30 (h953 baseline) is a MACRO-averaging artifact: small bio_gt_size per disease (often 1–2 biologics) means each bio hit contributes disproportionately to the per-disease r30 mean. Slot-for-slot (p30|type), biologics are LOWER precision in 17 of 18 categories; only endocrine (n=6, too small) inverts. h991's step-2 decision rule (‘categories where sm_p30 ≤ bio_p30 − 5pp’) yields ZERO qualifying categories (n≥50, bio_n≥10). Precision can’t be lifted by demoting SM slots as h991 proposed. **Valuable side finding (diagnostic):** within SM top-30, train_frequency × mechanism_support is a dominant precision gradient — f=1–2 no-mech slots hit at 7.5% vs f≥10+mech slots at 46.06% (6× range, pooled n=4783 vs 1359). This freq+mech gradient is the actionable precision signal surfaced by h991 and motivates h996 (tier-rule demote for low-freq no-mech SM) and strengthens h994 (in-window re-ranking). Also confirms h957’s global bio demote was directionally right on precision but failed ship gate because biologic GT is too recall-critical per disease. Raw: data/analysis/h991_sm_precision_gap.json + data/analysis/h991_run.txt.
hypotheses.result_metric: sm_p30|sm = 15.48%, bio_p30|bio = 5.64% (gap −9.85pp); 0/18 categories show SM < bio at n≥50; SM freq+mech crosstab 7.5% → 46.06% hit rate gradient

hypotheses.title: Per-disease GT-size calibrated p30 — is the p30 ceiling structural?
hypotheses.rationale: h953 shows p30=14.32% is extremely stable across all demotion regimes (±0.05pp). With expanded GT averaging ~57 drugs per disease, a perfect top-30 could hit p30 ≈ min(30,|GT|)/30 — so the p30 ceiling per disease depends on |GT|. Hypothesis: for diseases with |GT|<30, the absolute p30 ceiling is |GT|/30 (not 100%). Compute the p30 ceiling per disease and express baseline p30 as 'fraction of the achievable p30 ceiling'. If the ceiling is ~40%, then 14.32% → ~36% of ceiling — a more honest precision number. This reframes all precision-focused hypotheses.
steps: For each holdout disease, compute p30_ceiling = min(|GT|, 30) / 30.
Compute p30_fraction = (baseline top30 ∩ GT) / min(|GT|, 30).
Aggregate per-category and overall. Report p30, p30_ceiling, p30_fraction as the new triptych.
Document 'p30 is bounded above by GT density' as a metric-hygiene note in CLAUDE.md (similar to h954/h967 micro-vs-macro note).

hypotheses.title: Per-rank hit-rate audit — formalize the rank 31-200 tail-uniformity claim
hypotheses.rationale: h990 surfaces an unproven structural claim: the rank 31-200 tail of kNN predictions hits at a uniform background rate, which is why h953/h990 demote-and-refill is precision-neutral. Verify directly: for each rank r in 1..200, compute p(hit | rank=r) across all holdout disease-prediction pairs over 5 seeds. If the curve is flat (e.g. p(hit) ≈ 0.10-0.15) for r ∈ [31, 200], the claim holds and ALL future precision pivots must operate inside rank 1-30. If the curve drops sharply (e.g. p(hit, r=200) ≪ p(hit, r=31)), there IS quality differentiation in the tail and a smarter selection (not simple swap) might work.
steps: Reuse h953/h990 plumbing. For each holdout disease, fetch top_n=200, record per-rank hit indicator vs expanded GT.
Aggregate p(hit | rank) across all holdout pairs over 5 seeds.
Plot/report the rank-curve in 10-rank bins. Compute slope of p(hit) vs rank for ranks 31-200.
Decision: if |slope| < 0.05pp/rank, claim h990's tail-uniformity is structural and add to CLAUDE.md as a metric-hygiene note. If steeper, file h995 to re-explore tail-aware demotion.

hypotheses.title: In-window re-ranking: precision lift via signal-aware reorder of top-30, no in/out exchange
hypotheses.rationale: h953 + h990 jointly close the 'demote and refill from rank 31+' family: the kNN tail provides no differentiation for the swap. The remaining precision lever is RE-ORDERING within top-30 — keep the same 30 drugs, but lift hits to higher ranks using auxiliary features (target overlap, literature evidence level, ATC coherence). For per-disease p30 this changes nothing (top-30 membership is invariant), but for tier-precision (GOLDEN/HIGH/MEDIUM rules that cap at rank 5/10/20), in-window re-ranking can move hits into higher tiers and raise tier precision.
steps: For each holdout disease, fetch top-30 from baseline production predict() — record (drug_id, rank, score, hit).
Score each prediction with auxiliary features: target_overlap_count, literature_evidence_score, ATC L1 match w/ disease, drug_train_freq.
Train a logistic re-ranker on train-disease (drug, hit?) pairs using these features + original kNN score. 5-fold CV.
Apply re-ranker to holdout: compute new rank order, re-derive tier assignments via the existing tier rules.
Measure tier precision change vs baseline. Ship if any tier improves ≥+1pp without other tiers dropping ≥1pp.

hypotheses.title: Autoimmune biologic-mis-selection audit — bio_p30|bio only 13.9% vs sm 39.1%
hypotheses.rationale: h991 diagnostic (pooled 5 seeds, n=29 autoimmune diseases) shows a striking gap: sm_p30|sm=39.1% but bio_p30|bio=13.9% (−25.2pp). Autoimmune is a category where biologics ARE the gold-standard therapy class (anti-TNF, anti-IL6, anti-IL17, anti-IL23, CD20-depletion, JAK-inhibitors). A 13.9% hit rate on biologic slots means the kNN is surfacing the WRONG biologics — e.g. recommending anti-CD20 for a disease where anti-TNF is indicated, or oncology biologics instead of immunology biologics. Hypothesis: if we inspect which biologic *families* (by USAN stem: -mab vs -cept vs cytokine) are in top-30 vs the bio_gt for the same disease, we'll find systematic family misalignment. If confirmed, a ‘biologic-family-match’ filter (only keep top-30 biologics whose family matches any biologic in GT of the k=3 nearest neighbor diseases) should lift autoimmune bio_p30 without crashing bio_r30. Low effort diagnostic first.
steps: For each autoimmune holdout disease, list top-30 biologic picks and the bio_gt drugs; extract USAN-suffix family for each (mab, cept, kinra, ferax, etc.).
Compute family-match rate: fraction of top-30 biologics whose family appears in the disease's bio_gt. Also compute same for hits vs misses.
If family-match hit_rate > family-mismatch hit_rate by ≥3x, propose a biologic-family-match filter and measure on 5-seed holdout.
Ship gate: bio_p30|bio lift ≥5pp on autoimmune AND global bio_r30 drop ≤2pp.
hypotheses.result_metric: LOO target_match ratio 4.22x (≥3x gate met) BUT in-out filter would drop 16/32 autoimmune hits = -50% bio_r30 (ship cap -2pp violated 25x)
hypotheses.findings:
h995 audit on 5-seed h393 autoimmune holdout (266 biologic top-30 slots, 32 hits pooled):
Naive target_match showed ratio=inf (hr_miss=0%) across every category — a tautology signature (candidate drugs IN bio_gt trivially satisfy target_match since their targets are ⊂ gt_target_union).
Leave-one-out (LOO) de-biased re-analysis (h995b) cleaned the signal:
  - suffix_match LOO: 0.74x (signal REVERSED — -mab/-cept suffix is anti-predictive)
  - substem_match LOO: 1.58x (below 3x gate)
  - target_match LOO: 4.22x (31.37% match hit rate vs 7.44% miss; STILL above 3x gate)
Tautology load: 49.5% of original target_match=True hits (96/194) flip to False under LOO — half the naive signal was self-inclusion.

Ship gate FAILS on filter form: target_match_loo=True retains 16/32 autoimmune hits; target_match_loo=False retains 16/32. A filter that drops LOO=False biologics would halve bio_r30 on autoimmune (-50%, violating -2pp cap by 25x). Per-category LOO ratios (cancer 10.9x, cv 11.6x, hematological 24.2x, metabolic 7.8x) are similarly decorative — the filter would destroy recall everywhere.

Mechanism: half of autoimmune biologic HITS are target-unique (the candidate is the first mAb of its target family in bio_gt; e.g. first anti-IL4Rα in a derm/autoimmune disease) — exactly the kind of real hit an in-out filter cannot rescue. Same failure mode as h957 zero-overlap filter and the h953/h990 in/out-shuffle family.

Genuine signal is real: the 31.37% vs 7.44% LOO ratio confirms target-family sharing IS a 4.2x precision signal for autoimmune biologic slots. But the operationalization must be in-window re-rank or annotation, not in/out filter.

hypotheses.title: SM low-freq no-mech tier demote — 6x precision gradient within SM top-30
hypotheses.rationale: h991 diagnostic cross-tab (SM top-30 slots, pooled 5 seeds, n=26,564): hit rate ranges from 7.86% (f=1 no-mech) to 46.06% (f≥10 + mech) — a 6× gradient. Currently the tier system uses train_frequency and mechanism_support indirectly (via sub_reason paths) but does not have an explicit TIER-level rule that demotes SM predictions where f≤2 AND no mechanism_support to LOW or FILTER. Pooled 4,783 SM slots (~18% of all SM slots in top-30) fall in this bucket at 7.57% precision — below current LOW tier 10.0% and comparable to FILTER 6.8%. Test: add a tier-override rule 'SM AND train_frequency≤2 AND NOT mechanism_support → cap at LOW (force demotion from MEDIUM/HIGH)'. Measure on 5-seed h393: expect MEDIUM precision +0.5 to +1.5pp and LOW precision approximately flat (since demoted slots were already low-quality).
steps: In a copy of _assign_confidence_tier, add rule before tier assignment: if drug is SM AND train_frequency≤2 AND NOT mechanism_support, cap final tier at LOW.
Run h393 evaluator 5 seeds; compare pre/post tier precisions.
Ship gate: MEDIUM precision +≥0.5pp AND LOW precision drop ≤1pp AND no tier-ordering inversions.
Audit: count tier demotions per tier to confirm rule targets MEDIUM slots (not already-LOW).
hypotheses.findings: INVALIDATED at precondition — existing tier system already handles the signal. 5-seed h393 pooled tier distribution of SM f≤2 no-mech slots (n=4,740 total): GOLDEN 0, HIGH 35 (94.29% hit rate, 33/35 — genuine high-precision), MEDIUM 0, LOW 86 (3.49%), FILTER 4,619 (6.02%). **99.3% of target slots are already at LOW or FILTER.** The proposed rule would destroy 33 legitimate HIGH hits (94% precision!) for zero MEDIUM lift (0 MEDIUM slots to demote). The h991 7.57% pooled hit rate was an across-tier AVERAGE; the tier system already correctly segregates the low-quality bulk (FILTER 6.02%) from the rare high-precision overrides (HIGH 94.29%). The 35 HIGH slots presumably survive via explicit promotion rules (hierarchy, mech×rank≤5, cancer_same_type, etc.) that beat the f≤2-no-mech default; these rules correctly recognize legitimate HIGH-confidence preds even when surface features look weak. **Lesson:** whenever a slot-level precision signal looks exploitable for tier rules, first measure the tier distribution of target slots — cheap rule-out check that saves implementation effort. Raw: data/analysis/h996_precondition_tier_distribution.json + data/analysis/h996_precondition_run.txt.
hypotheses.result_metric: 99.3% of target slots already at LOW/FILTER; 35 HIGH survivors hit at 94.29% (would be destroyed by rule); 0 MEDIUM slots to demote — ship gate unreachable

hypotheses.title: Macro-averaged r30 amplifies small-|GT| noise — replace bio_r30 headline with |GT|-weighted version
hypotheses.rationale: h991 exposed that bio_r30=30.31% > overall_r30=19.79% (h953 headline) was driven by macro-averaging over diseases with tiny bio_gt (often 1–2 biologics). When bio_gt=1, a single bio hit contributes 100% to that disease's bio_r30; when bio_gt=20, the same single hit contributes 5%. Macro-mean makes the tiny-|GT| cases dominate the headline. This drove three false narratives: h951 'biologic failure dissolved' (actually: biologics are fine on recall but lower on slot-level precision), h953 hypothesis framing ('precision pivot should be on SM'), and implicitly h906/h921/h924 motivations. Fix: compute MICRO-averaged bio_r30 = (total bio hits across diseases) / (total bio_gt across diseases) alongside macro. Report both in research_spec and CLAUDE.md. Predict: micro bio_r30 ≪ macro bio_r30 because large-|GT| diseases (where biologics ARE treatment class, like autoimmune) have the lowest hit rates.

Compare to the macro numbers; quantify how much of the +10pp bio_r30 > overall_r30 gap collapses.
Update CLAUDE.md 'Key Metrics' section with both macro and micro bio_r30.
Update research_spec baseline table to flag the metric-mix pitfall (cf h967).

hypotheses.title: What overrides keep the 35 HIGH SM f≤2 no-mech slots at 94.3% precision?
hypotheses.rationale: h996 precondition revealed 35 HIGH-tier SM predictions with train_frequency≤2 AND NOT mechanism_support across 5 seeds, hitting at 94.29% (33/35). These shouldn't look high-confidence by default heuristics but are promoted by an explicit rule (hierarchy, comp_to_base, cancer_same_type, transe_high_promotion, etc.). Identify WHICH sub_reason paths promote these to HIGH; the over-representation of 94% precision suggests the overriding signal is very strong and potentially transferable. If a single path (e.g. hierarchy_cv_anticoag) dominates, it validates a pre-existing rule and we can annotate. If multiple weaker paths contribute, we may discover a composite signal worth adding as an explicit promotion rule elsewhere.

Tabulate: which sub_reasons surface these 35 HIGH survivors?
For the top sub_reasons, check whether the same sub_reason is under-promoted elsewhere (f≥3, has-mech) — possible new promotion target.

hypotheses.title: LOW→FILTER demote for SM f≤2 no-mech sub-population (3.49% pooled)
hypotheses.rationale: h996 precondition: the 86 LOW-tier SM f≤2 no-mech slots hit at 3.49% vs LOW-tier overall 10.07% — a 2.9x deficit. Confidence interval is wide (3/86, 95% CI ~[0.7%, 9.9%]) but center is well below LOW. If these preds are identifiable by a clean rule, they could be demoted to FILTER. Small expected tier lift (~86 preds/5-seed on ~12,000 LOW preds = 0.7% of LOW volume), but the precondition data is already collected so marginal effort is near-zero. Ship gate: LOW precision +≥0.2pp AND FILTER precision ≤ current (don't contaminate FILTER).

Verify 95% CI of 3.49% hit rate excludes 10% (LOW tier average).
Add tier-override: LOW AND SM AND f≤2 AND no mech → FILTER. Measure on 5-seed h393.

hypotheses.title: In-window biologic family-match re-rank (no in/out exchange)
hypotheses.rationale: h995/h995b showed biologic-family target-match (LOO) is a 4.22x autoimmune precision signal (31.37% match hit vs 7.44% miss) but filter form loses 50% of bio_r30 because half the hits are target-unique (first-in-family mAbs). In-window re-rank avoids that failure: within the top-30 biologic slots, BUMP target_match_LOO=True candidates up by +1 rank tier and DEMOTE target_match_LOO=False biologics down by 1 rank, KEEPING all 30 slots. This preserves bio_r30 (no hits dropped from top-30) while concentrating the match-family hits at lower ranks → higher tier precision. Ship gate: bio_r30 drop ≤0.5pp AND bio-tier distribution shifts ≥1 biologic/seed from MEDIUM→HIGH (or FILTER→LOW). Aligns with h994 in-window re-rank family.
steps: Compute per-prediction target_match_LOO flag at inference time using bio_gt of the disease's k=3 kNN neighbors (not disease's own bio_gt — that leaks at inference). h995b used own-disease bio_gt; that's only valid for audit, not for prediction.
Implement in-window rank shift: biologic with target_match_LOO=True in top-30 gets rank shift -1, False gets +1. Tiers are then recomputed.
5-seed h393 holdout: measure bio_p30, bio_r30, global tier precisions (GOLDEN/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/FILTER) vs baseline.
Ship if bio_r30 drop ≤0.5pp AND at least one tier lifts by ≥1pp.

Only 60 of 3,570 biologic slots changed tier across seeds (1.7%) — rank thresholds at 5/10/15/20 mean ±1 shift rarely crosses a boundary. Biologic tier distribution hardly moved: GOLDEN 41/53→42/54, HIGH 19/32→20/33, MEDIUM 8/81→9/83, LOW -43n, FILTER +39n. bio_r30 unchanged (29.20%, top-30 membership invariant by construction). Also: 2,786/3,570 (78%) biologics have target_match_LOO_neighbor=False — neighbor bio_gt is too narrow a universe per h1002. Among the 60 tier moves, high-precision promotions exist (FILTER→GOLDEN 1/1, LOW→HIGH 1/1) but numerically too sparse to lift any tier. The dominant move is LOW→FILTER (44 preds, 4.5% hit rate — legitimate demotes but no tier lift). Filter-form biologic precision family remains closed (h953, h957, h990, h995, h1000, h1002).

hypotheses.title: Biologic family-match deliverable annotation column (audit signal, no tier change)

Ryland and collaborators can use it to triage predictions at review time without the filter costing us 50% of biologic recall. h995b showed 4.22x LOO signal on autoimmune and 5.67x-24.22x across cancer/cv/metabolic/hematological — these annotations will consistently correlate with expert agreement. Mirrors h968 annotation philosophy over filter philosophy.

Add columns `biologic_target_family_match`, `biologic_shared_targets` to the XLSX.

hypotheses.title: First-in-family biologic GT gap audit — unique-target hits
hypotheses.rationale: h995b's LOO analysis revealed 16 autoimmune biologic HITS where the candidate was the ONLY biologic with its target set in bio_gt (target_match_loo=False). If these are novel first-in-family mAbs/biologics (anti-IL4Rα, anti-IL5, anti-IL23), their uniqueness is exactly the signal the filter cannot see. Hypothesis: enumerate the 16 unique-target hits, characterize them (drug family, disease, literature support), and check whether they share kNN-neighbor reasoning (i.e. the disease's kNN-nearest neighbor diseases contain OTHER biologics with the same target). If yes, propose augmenting bio_gt at inference time with k=3 neighbor bio_gt before computing target_match — rescuing most of the 50% hit loss while keeping the filter form.
steps: Extract the 16 autoimmune hits with target_match=True BUT target_match_loo=False from h995_slot_records.json.
For each, look up the drug's target set + disease's top-3 kNN neighbors' bio_gt union of targets.
Compute 'neighbor-augmented' target_match_loo — would this rescue the 16 hits?
If ≥12/16 rescued, propose h1003 implementing neighbor-augmented filter.

hypotheses.findings: h1002 neighbor-augmented (k=3 kNN) bio_gt union tested as rescue for the 16 autoimmune unique-target hits (target_match_loo=False, hit=True) surfaced by h995b. Only 1/16 (6.2%) flipped True under neighbor augmentation: Corticotropin → lupus nephritis (seed 123). The other 15 are genuinely target-unique ACROSS the disease's full DRKG neighborhood — e.g. Adalimumab→non-behcets uveitis, Tocilizumab→temporal arteritis, Rituximab→microscopic polyangiitis, Anakinra+Canakinumab→familial mediterranean fever, Abatacept→SLE. Their kNN neighbors have no anti-TNF/anti-IL6R/anti-IL1/anti-CD20/CTLA4-Ig in expanded GT. Structural conclusion: at least 50% of autoimmune biologic HITS (16/32) are target-unique at the disease-neighborhood level. No filter-side augmentation can rescue them. Filter-form biologic precision improvements on autoimmune are STRUCTURALLY capped at halving bio_r30 (-50pp). This closes filter-style biologic precision pivots as a family (h953 biologic prior, h990 neighbor prior, h957 zero-overlap, h995 family-match, h1002 neighbor-augmented all fail). Remaining viable surfaces: in-window re-rank (h994, h1000) and deliverable annotation (h1001).

hypotheses.title: GraphSAGE Full Retrain — Replace Node2Vec Embeddings for All 1,463 Evaluable Diseases
hypotheses.rationale: h922 (original) tested GraphSAGE as inductive inference for 22 island diseases — pilot failed (0/22 top-30 hits via naive neighbour-mean) and the target pool is small anyway. That was the wrong experiment. The real value of a GNN on DRKG is LEARNING BETTER EMBEDDINGS FOR ALL 1,463 evaluable diseases — replacing the 256-d Node2Vec embeddings currently used by production kNN. Node2Vec captures random-walk structure but not message-passing semantics; a trained GraphSAGE (or HGT / RGCN) should learn multi-hop paths kNN misses, pushing per-drug R@30 toward the ~60% DRKG Oracle ceiling (currently ~37% for kNN). This is the single biggest lever on the 37->60 gap that is not blocked by external data or human review.

hypotheses.findings: DON'T PRODUCTIONIZE GraphSAGE as a drop-in Node2Vec replacement. Training converged cleanly (val AUC 0.9889 on link prediction, early stop at epoch 24/50, 40 min on RTX 4090, $0.40 spent), and produced 94,247 x 256-d embeddings. But side-by-side evaluation (h393 5-seed + positive controls) shows a tier-wide regression: HIGH -13.4pp (80.4->67.0), MEDIUM -12.8pp (39.9->27.1), LOW -3.6pp, FILTER -2.9pp. GOLDEN rose +6.0pp (82.6->88.6) but std doubled (4.0->7.9), suggesting small-n noise rather than real gain. Positive controls fell 8/20 -> 4/20 in top-30, with specific regressions on Rituximab->MS (55 HIGH -> not top-100), Sildenafil->PAH, Bupropion->smoking, Riluzole->ALS. ROOT CAUSE: tier rules are calibrated to Node2Vec-specific kNN neighbourhoods. Swapping embeddings changes which predictions hit which rules, which breaks the tier-precision contract. GraphSAGE isn't 'worse' absolutely; it's miscalibrated with the current 30-rule confidence system. Paths forward if we want to revisit (not priorities today): (1) train GraphSAGE supervised on treatment edges (different objective than unsupervised link-prediction), (2) recalibrate the entire 30-rule system against GraphSAGE-generated kNN neighbourhoods (huge effort, ~800 iterations of the original confidence work), (3) use GraphSAGE as a secondary fusion signal rather than primary embedding (rank fusion), (4) try a different GNN architecture (HGT, RGCN) that captures heterogeneous relations that SAGE's single-relation collapse loses. Artifacts preserved: data/embeddings/graphsage_256_*.npy, data/analysis/h922_v2_vs_node2vec.json, data/analysis/positive_controls_graphsage.json. The OPEN_CURE_EMBEDDINGS_PREFIX env-var hook remains in production_predictor.py for future experiments.

hypotheses.rationale: Path B of the 37->60 pivot. LINCS L1000 encodes 'what transcriptomic state does a drug induce' across ~20k compounds on ~70 cell lines. Combined with disease expression signatures from GEO/ARCHS4, drugs whose signatures REVERSE a disease's dysregulation are candidate treatments. This is orthogonal to graph structure — a drug can treat a disease via expression reversal even when kNN has no neighbours to inform from. Literature (CMap / L1000) shows 20-30% hit rates on known repurposing pairs using reversal alone. Expected contribution: +5-10pp on biologics and rare diseases where graph signal is weak. Critically complementary, not competitive, with kNN.

hypotheses.rationale: h1101 surfaced drug_cancer_types[Dantrolene]={'solid_tumor'} even though Dantrolene is a muscle relaxant / RyR modulator with no oncology role. Likely traces to a single DRKG edge (cancer-adjacent paper co-mentioning Dantrolene). If the drug_cancer_types mapping has similar artifacts for other non-cancer drugs, it might incorrectly route predictions through cancer-specific tier paths (cancer_same_type, cancer_targeted_therapy, cancer_no_gt). Audit: scan drug_cancer_types for drugs with train_frequency >= 5 whose GT diseases are 0% cancer-category — those are candidates for cleanup.
steps: Load drug_cancer_types mapping from production_predictor
For each drug, compute: cancer_types_count, gt_diseases_count, cancer_gt_fraction (% of GT diseases that are cancer-category)
Flag drugs with cancer_types_count >= 1 AND cancer_gt_fraction == 0 AND train_freq >= 3 as likely artifacts
Spot-check 10 of the flagged drugs against FDA / DrugBank indication labels
If the artifact rate is >= 30%, propose a cleanup rule: require at least one cancer-category GT disease before assigning cancer_types
Before shipping: ensure no regression in cancer tier precision via h393 holdout

hypotheses.title: Paper Section 3.5 audit — validate every retrospectively-corroborated prediction
hypotheses.rationale: h1101 showed that the Dantrolene row of Paper Section 3.5 conflated cohort (HF) with outcome (VT). There are N other rows in the same table that were never re-checked against model output. Audit every row: does the model actually predict the claimed (drug, disease) at any rank? If not, either the disease label needs the same kind of correction, or the row needs to move out of 'retrospectively corroborated'. Mirror the positive-control script methodology — exact drug name, exact disease string, rank/tier/sub_reason for each.
steps: Extract every row of Paper Section 3.5 into a machine-readable list (drug, disease_claim, rct_source) saved to data/analysis/h1107_section_3_5_claims.json
For each row, call p.predict(disease_claim, top_n=500, include_filtered=True) and check if the drug is present; record rank, tier, sub_reason, in_gt, mechanism_support

For rows where the drug is not predicted for the claimed disease, search for related diseases in the same category/family (e.g., for 'heart failure' also check 'ventricular tachycardia', 'arrhythmia') and report what WAS found
Update paper_v2_errata.md with every required relabel
If >= 3 rows need errata, escalate to Interactive for a preprint re-submission decision
