kNN collaborative filtering is structurally a repurposing engine: 100% of predictions are for drugs that treat at least one training disease. No novel-drug predictions exist. All holdout hits are genuine cross-disease transfer.

CS inflation quantified: HIGH tier is 69% corticosteroids. Non-CS HIGH = 48.5% (vs 58.8% total). MEDIUM barely affected (6% CS, non-CS 34.8% vs 36.5%). Tier ordering preserved for non-CS. Report CS-free precision as supplemental metric.

learnings.learning: Therapeutic islands fail not because of drug uniqueness (67-100% shared) but because kNN neighbors use DIFFERENT drug classes (mean overlap 0.3-7.2 vs 6.2-22.6 for high performers). Embedding similarity is fine; treatment paradigm is different. Alternative signals (TransE, gene overlap) cannot generate NEW predictions. System still works for some islands via hierarchy/ATC rules (ADHD: 18 MEDIUM+, PAH: 11 HIGH). Holdout metric is misleading for self-referential diseases.
learnings.implication: No rescue possible within kNN architecture. Need non-kNN prediction strategies (drug class expansion, literature mining) for island diseases. Consider correcting holdout metric to exclude self-referential diseases.

learnings.learning: Self-referential diseases (31.6% of diseases, 100% self-ref) drag holdout precision down by 3-5pp across all tiers. True non-self-ref MEDIUM precision is 40.5% (not 37.6%), achieving the 40% target deemed unachievable in h561. For <50% self-ref diseases, MEDIUM reaches 44.0%. Self-ref diseases contribute 29% of LOW and 34% of FILTER predictions with minimal hits, inflating the denominator.
learnings.implication: Report corrected precision alongside uncorrected for accurate quality assessment. The system is better than previously thought for discoverable diseases.

learnings.learning: Paradigm mismatch (embedding sim - drug Jaccard with kNN neighbors) predicts holdout precision independently of self-referentiality (r=0.032 with self-ref) and GT size. Drug Jaccard (partial r=0.428 controlling for GT size) is the key component. BUT the signal is GT-dependent (circular at prediction time). Valid as annotation but cannot be used for novel disease predictions.
learnings.implication: Need GT-free proxy for drug Jaccard. DRKG edge-based similarity might approximate it. Paradigm mismatch quartile can annotate disease prediction reliability in deliverable.

learnings.learning: DRKG gene associations cannot proxy drug Jaccard (treatment similarity). Gene biology ≠ treatment paradigm. 63% of diseases share zero genes with kNN neighbors. GT-free mismatch collapses to embed_sim (r=0.996). Symptom Jaccard shows promise (partial_r=0.296) but Hetionet symptom coverage too sparse (39/312 diseases). HPO may extend this.
learnings.implication: Treatment paradigm information requires actual treatment data, not molecular biology. External sources (HPO phenotypes, ATC hierarchy, clinical guidelines) are the most promising GT-free proxies.

learnings.learning: HPO phenotype similarity predicts drug Jaccard 4.5x better than gene overlap (r=0.390 vs 0.086). Clinical phenotype captures treatment paradigm better than molecular biology. But incremental value beyond GT+embed_sim is only 0.9% R². HPO covers 26.3% of holdout diseases — better than Hetionet symptoms (12.5%) but still sparse.
learnings.implication: Phenotype-based similarity is the best GT-free proxy for treatment paradigm. To fully exploit, would need comprehensive phenotype data for more diseases. DisGeNET/OMIM phenotype annotations could expand coverage.

learnings.learning: ATC hierarchy is the best proxy for drug Jaccard (L3 r=0.737), far exceeding gene overlap (r=0.086) and HPO (r=0.390). But it adds ZERO signal beyond drug Jaccard (partial_r=-0.013). ATC is a noisy version of drug Jaccard, not an independent signal. This closes the search for GT-free treatment paradigm proxies within DRKG: no DRKG-derived signal can independently predict treatment similarity.
learnings.implication: Treatment paradigm information is ONLY available from treatment data itself. No amount of biological (genes), phenotypic (HPO), or therapeutic classification (ATC) information provides an INDEPENDENT signal beyond drug Jaccard. The paradigm mismatch concept (h583) is fundamentally a GT-dependent metric. Future quality signals must come from entirely external sources (clinical practice guidelines, expert curation, or RWD prescribing patterns).

learnings.learning: Hetionet disease-resembles edges are 80% already in kNN top-20 (the embedding captures them). Resembles neighbors have LOWER drug overlap (0.036 vs kNN 0.045) and provide only 0.2 unique GT hits per disease. No augmentation value — kNN already uses this information.
learnings.implication: DRKG-derived auxiliary signals (resembles, gene overlap, HPO phenotype) are all subsumed by or redundant with what Node2Vec embeddings already capture. Any improvement must come from truly external data sources.

learnings.learning: Composite quality score combining disease-level signals (holdout precision, self-ref) with prediction-level signals (rank, TransE, gene overlap) provides +2.6pp over kNN rank alone for MEDIUM tier prioritization. Disease-level signals are the key addition that h443 (prediction-level composite) missed.
learnings.implication: For practical experiment prioritization, composite scores outperform single-signal sorting. This is an annotation/prioritization signal, not a tier promotion signal.

learnings.learning: 50% of high-evidence non-CS/non-antibiotic novel predictions (rank<=3, same-category GT>=3) are actually FDA-approved GT gaps. Posaconazole alone had 5 missing fungal disease indications. GT incompleteness inflates the 'novel prediction' count and deflates measured precision.
learnings.implication: Before claiming predictions are novel repurposing discoveries, systematically check for GT gaps. Drug families (triazoles, taxanes, etc.) tend to have correlated GT gaps - fixing one drug in the family suggests checking all others.

learnings.learning: Antifungal GT is 85% complete (23/27 checked pairs already present). Posaconazole gaps (h593) were an outlier. Cancer drugs likely have larger GT gaps than antifungals.
learnings.implication: GT gap detection has diminishing returns for well-covered drug families. Focus on cancer drugs (h597) where subtype-level GT is less complete.

learnings.learning: Cancer chemotherapy GT is more complete than expected. Cisplatin/gemcitabine/carboplatin already have 29-39 cancer subtypes in GT. GT gaps are concentrated in newer/specialty drugs (bortezomib, bevacizumab) and rare cancer subtypes. Cumulative GT expansion (h593-h597): 18 pairs, MEDIUM +1.2pp.
learnings.implication: GT expansion has diminishing returns. The 18 most obvious gaps are fixed. Remaining gaps require drug-specific FDA label cross-referencing rather than systematic class-level detection.

learnings.learning: CANCER_TARGETED_THERAPY was incomplete — missing anti-target mAbs (HER2/EGFR/VEGFR), PARP inhibitors, and BTK inhibitors. These drug classes have 6.1% holdout vs 40.2% for remaining cancer_same_type (34.1pp gap). Adding 15 drugs improved MEDIUM by +3.3pp.
learnings.implication: When creating drug class lists, check ALL drug classes in the same therapeutic area, not just the most obvious ones. mAbs and novel targeted agents are easily missed because they have different naming conventions than small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

learnings.learning: Within-antibacterial spectrum matching (gram+/gram-) is NOT actionable. Only 22 mismatches (4.8%), 53% are medically false positives (aminoglycoside synergy, azithromycin anti-inflammatory use, 1st-gen ceph UTI coverage). The broad antimicrobial-pathogen mismatch (h560) is sufficient.
learnings.implication: Drug spectrum classification is too nuanced for rule-based approaches. Many antibiotics have secondary activities (synergy, anti-inflammatory, biofilm disruption) that rule-based classification misses. Only broad category mismatches (antibacterial→viral/fungal/parasitic) are clean enough for automated filtering.

learnings.learning: Standard MEDIUM analysis: metabolic (10.3%) is the only cleanly demotable category remaining. Respiratory (22.3%) and endocrine (24.5%) are borderline — between LOW and MEDIUM. The MEDIUM_DEMOTED_CATEGORIES check intercepts ALL predictions before ATC coherent rescue, so adding categories there also blocks ATC coherent pathway. Only add categories that are already excluded from ATC coherent or where the combined precision is clearly LOW.
learnings.implication: Future MEDIUM demotion attempts must account for interaction with ATC coherent pathway. Categories NOT in ATC_COHERENT_EXCLUDED will lose their ATC rescue predictions when added to MEDIUM_DEMOTED_CATEGORIES.

learnings.learning: Standard MEDIUM infectious (22.7% holdout) is heterogeneous: tetracycline class performs well (32.3%) while fluoroquinolone (11.4%) and macrolide (10.6%) underperform. Per-drug analysis shows tetracycline-the-drug has 0% holdout (vs doxycycline 35.4%, minocycline 36.6%). Legacy antibiotics (tetracycline, erythromycin) contribute most false positives but per-drug n is too small for reliable demotion rules.
learnings.implication: Diminishing returns on MEDIUM demotion. Individual drug holdout requires n>30/drug for reliability. Standard MEDIUM infectious at 22.7% is below MEDIUM avg (41.3%) but above LOW (15.1%) — demoting the entire category would lose genuine MEDIUM predictions from doxycycline/minocycline.

learnings.learning: ATC coherent rescue pathway has highly heterogeneous quality across categories. Only infectious (n=41/seed, 27.6%) is statistically reliable. Psychiatric confirmed below MEDIUM (17.2%, p<0.001). Most categories have n<5/seed — too small for reliable holdout. Category-specific ATC coherent analysis requires pooling across categories or very large holdout.
learnings.implication: Per-category ATC coherent quality varies from 0% to 30%. Should systematically evaluate ALL MEDIUM sub-pathways × categories for remaining low-quality pockets.

learnings.learning: CRITICAL: predictor.ground_truth has only 3,070 pairs (DRKG-derived). expanded_ground_truth.json has 59,584 pairs (19x more). Using wrong GT for holdout eval gives systematically LOW precision — cancer_same_type shows 11.8% vs 37.7% with correct GT. ALWAYS use expanded GT (as h393 evaluator does).
learnings.implication: All previous inline holdout evaluations in this session (h606, h611) used wrong GT. Rankings between sub-pathways are preserved but absolute numbers are wrong. The h606 psychiatric ATC exclusion was independently validated by h393 (correct GT) so that change stands.

learnings.learning: Expanded GT has 19x more pairs. Cancer=13.2x ratio (highest). Per-tier inflation: GOLDEN +12.9pp, HIGH +16.8pp, MEDIUM +15.4pp, LOW +6.3pp. Higher tiers benefit proportionally more from expanded GT.
learnings.implication: Inline evaluations must ALWAYS use expanded GT. The internal GT significantly understates system quality. Cancer predictions especially affected.

learnings.learning: Internal GT (3,070 pairs) systematically underestimates hierarchy group precision. With expanded GT (59,584 pairs), 4 hierarchy groups (RA, colitis, coronary, arrhythmia) are GOLDEN-quality despite being classified HIGH based on internal GT analysis. Per-group holdout validation is essential for tier assignment.
learnings.implication: All future tier decisions should use expanded GT for evaluation. Category-level precision analysis can miss group-level quality differences.

learnings.learning: Both internal and expanded GT contain non-therapeutic associations (diagnostic use of FDG PET coded as treatment indication). 70.1% of FILTER GT hits come from internal GT. Contamination is minimal (3.3%) and does not affect tier ordering. Disease categorization errors exist for pleural mesothelioma (respiratory instead of cancer) and retinoblastoma (ophthalmic instead of cancer).
learnings.implication: GT quality is adequate for tier evaluation. Disease categorization fixes could rescue a small number of predictions but are low priority.

learnings.learning: Internal GT (3,070 pairs) systematically underestimates CV drug precision. Expanded GT (59,584) reveals genuine CV drugs have 30.9% holdout in CV demotion group. Drug-class stratification cleanly separates CV pharmacotherapy (30.9%) from non-CV drugs (4.6%).
learnings.implication: All MEDIUM_DEMOTED_CATEGORIES should be re-evaluated with expanded GT. Category-level demotions may be hiding drug-class-specific quality that only appears with complete GT.

learnings.learning: Category demotions are well-calibrated for all non-CV categories even with expanded GT. The CV rescue worked because anticoagulants have high n (14.2/seed). Other categories lack a dominant genuine drug class with sufficient holdout volume.
learnings.implication: MEDIUM_DEMOTED_CATEGORIES exhausted for drug-class rescue. Further MEDIUM improvements need promotions or new signals, not demotion reversals.

learnings.learning: MEDIUM tier is well-calibrated at sub-pathway level with expanded GT. Metabolic predictions with target_overlap leak through to MEDIUM and have 48.9% holdout — correctly promoted. All sub-pathways with n>=3/seed are above MEDIUM threshold.
learnings.implication: MEDIUM tier optimization is complete. No further demotions possible. Focus on HIGH/GOLDEN improvements or annotation quality.

learnings.learning: HIGH tier variance (±13.5%) is structural — driven by which hierarchy-matching diseases end up in holdout. Cannot be reduced without stratified splitting. comp_to_base_high_87 shows 0% holdout but n=5/seed is too small for action.
learnings.implication: HIGH variance is irreducible with current holdout methodology. Report confidence intervals rather than trying to fix. Consider stratified holdout for future evaluations.

learnings.learning: Disease-subtype analysis within blanket category demotions can find rescuable populations. Immune-mediated vs genetic/structural hematological diseases cleanly separate (48.4% vs 3.8%). The h622 closure was drug-class level; disease-subtype level is a different and more successful approach.
learnings.implication: Apply disease-subtype analysis to other demoted categories (metabolic, GI, neurological). Focus on subtypes with distinct drug classes AND non-self-referential diseases.

learnings.learning: Expanded GT resolves TransE MEDIUM blocker: internal GT showed 34.7% (below HIGH), expanded GT shows 56.5% (above HIGH). The 19.3pp differential over non-TransE MEDIUM is constant regardless of GT. TransE+mechanism+rank<=10 reaches GOLDEN-level (71.9%). Mechanism+rank<=10 alone = 52.5% ± 4.4% (HIGH-level with very low variance).
learnings.implication: Signal combination stratification within MEDIUM reveals HIGH/GOLDEN-quality subsets. The key insight: expanded GT doesn't just inflate precision uniformly — it preferentially lifts predictions with strong signals. TransE+mechanism predictions benefit more from expanded GT than no-signal predictions.

learnings.learning: TransE MEDIUM → HIGH promotion is safe with strict criteria (mechanism OR rank<=5, non-CS). 56.1% holdout for promoted predictions. HIGH precision INCREASES (+0.3pp) while variance DECREASES (-1.3%). Counter-intuitively, adding predictions can improve tier precision by rebalancing the composition.
learnings.implication: CLOSED direction #2 (within-tier reranking) should be revisited as CLOSED direction for PROMOTION (not reranking). TransE promotion works because expanded GT revealed the signal was always there but underestimated.

learnings.learning: Mechanism+rank<=10 within MEDIUM is NOT independently promotable. The 52.5% holdout is an average of heterogeneous groups: some would benefit (cancer_same_type 40.2%, target_overlap 51.2%) but others are correctly at MEDIUM/LOW (procedural artifacts 24, metabolic demotions 15). Mechanism is already incorporated into tier logic, so MEDIUM+mechanism predictions are there because they lack OTHER promoting signals.
learnings.implication: Signal combination analysis (h629) is valuable for IDENTIFYING opportunities but each promotion must be validated against tier_rule context. TransE was safe because it's an INDEPENDENT model. Mechanism is NOT independent of the tier system.

learnings.learning: CV rescue without mechanism was 22.5% (borderline LOW). Mechanism gating improved MEDIUM by +2.7pp. Rescue rules should be gated on mechanism when holdout shows significant split.
learnings.implication: Check all rescue rules for mechanism split. Also: ALL remaining non-CS MEDIUM are rank 16-20.

learnings.learning: ATC coherent exclusions have minimal holdout impact because GT recomputation reduces train_frequency below the freq>=3 threshold for borderline drugs. The change only affects full-data precision and deliverable quality.
learnings.implication: ATC coherent holdout evaluation is insensitive to category exclusions. Focus on deliverable impact for these changes.

learnings.learning: Cancer same-type rank 16-20 has 31.9% holdout — below MEDIUM avg but 2x LOW avg. Many predictions are medically legitimate (FDA-approved drugs for the correct cancer type). Decided not to demote.
learnings.implication: 31.9% is a grey zone between MEDIUM and LOW. Quartile annotations provide better differentiation than discrete tier demotion.

learnings.learning: Cancer same-type rank 11-15 at 55.8% was inflated by n=1 outlier (seed 42 at 100%). Excluding the outlier: 44.7% ± 8.6%, not promotable to HIGH. Always exclude n=1 outlier seeds before reporting means.
learnings.implication: Small n with outlier seeds can inflate means by 10+ pp. Report medians or exclude n<3 seeds.

learnings.learning: Literature validation (medical knowledge + ClinicalTrials.gov) provides independent quality assessment for holdout-invisible predictions. ATC coherent predictions: 72.7% literature-validated precision (61.9% GT + 10.8% ESTABLISHED/CLINICAL). Holdout invisibility is a methodological limitation, not quality issue. ClinicalTrials.gov only captures 9.2% of standard antimicrobial uses — most are in prescribing info/guidelines.
learnings.implication: Literature validation can supplement holdout for small-n sub-reasons. Spectrum-level antimicrobial rules could catch 13 wrong-spectrum predictions. 21 GT gaps identified.

learnings.learning: GT gap expansion for holdout-invisible predictions has zero holdout impact (as expected). The value is in GT quality improvement and full-data precision accuracy. For holdout-affecting GT gaps, need to target predictions that survive holdout freq threshold. Diminishing returns: most common antibiotic/antifungal GT gaps are now covered.
learnings.implication: Future GT gap efforts should focus on categories that affect holdout (non-ATC-coherent predictions).

learnings.learning: Anti-VEGF drugs (bevacizumab, ramucirumab) have high cross-cancer transferability because VEGF angiogenesis is a pan-tumor hallmark. kNN correctly captures this. Bevacizumab LOW predictions (rank 5-30) are surprisingly well-validated (71.4% CLINICAL_EVIDENCE) suggesting systematic underranking. Key GT gaps: bevacizumab→lung cancer (FDA 2006!), ramucirumab→lung cancer (FDA 2014). Literature validation hits ClinicalTrials.gov better for cancer drugs than for antibiotics (13 lung trials vs 0 for most antibiotic pairs).
learnings.implication: Cancer drug literature validation via ClinicalTrials.gov is more effective than antibiotic validation. Anti-VEGF LOW predictions may deserve reexamination for promotion.

learnings.learning: Systematic GT gap search across HIGH predictions is high-ROI: 54 pairs yielded +3.2pp HIGH, +0.4pp MEDIUM. Key gap patterns: (1) DOACs→atrial flutter (4 FDA drugs, all gaps), (2) cancer drugs→specific subtypes, (3) common antibiotics→prescribing-info uses, (4) basic SOC missing (thyroid hormone→hypothyroidism). GT gap search is more impactful for HIGH (3.2pp) than MEDIUM (0.4pp) because HIGH predictions are higher confidence and more likely to be true positives with missing GT.
learnings.implication: Further GT gap search should focus on remaining 200+ HIGH novel predictions. DOAC gaps suggest systematic mapping issues (disease term variants). Cancer drug gaps cluster around specific subtypes not in reference DBs.

learnings.learning: CS HIGH novel predictions are 97.2% medically acceptable (vs 62.3% non-CS). CS domination of HIGH novel is a QUALITY feature, not an artifact. Found 2 bugs: (1) diabetes insipidus matched via "diabetes" substring in comp_to_base (9 wrong HIGH preds), (2) 6 false GT entries from NLP misinterpreting "secondary causes to exclude" as indications in Every Cure data.
learnings.implication: Always validate HIGH novel predictions by medical literature — it catches both bugs and GT gaps. NLP-extracted GT databases have systematic errors from differential diagnosis patterns. CS predictions should NOT be treated as lower quality than non-CS.

learnings.learning: CS safety audit: TEN (no RCT evidence, infection risk), PAP (74% deteriorate, macrophage suppression), OSA (HR 1.40 increased risk) are harmful. Dacryocystitis is legitimate adjunctive use. CRITICAL BUG: duplicate dict keys in INVERSE_INDICATION_PAIRS silently overwrote IPF/glaucoma/osteoporosis filters.
learnings.implication: Always check for duplicate dict keys when adding new inverse indication entries. Python silently takes the last entry.

learnings.learning: 18 false GT entries found from 2 NLP error patterns: (1) 'secondary causes should be excluded' boilerplate in lipid drug labels (17 entries), (2) 'must be excluded' differential diagnosis in nafarelin label (1 entry). Lipid drug labels ALWAYS list hypothyroidism, diabetes, nephrotic syndrome, dysproteinemia, liver disease as exclusion criteria.
learnings.implication: NLP extraction of FDA labels has systematic false positives wherever diseases are mentioned in exclusion/differential contexts. Standard boilerplate affects all drugs in a class.

learnings.learning: Amphotericin B's antiparasitic activity is narrow (Leishmania only), not blanket. _DUAL_ACTIVITY tags should match actual spectrum, not broad class. Use _LEGITIMATE_CROSS_PAIRS for specific exceptions rather than broad dual-activity tags.
learnings.implication: Review other dual-activity drugs for similarly narrow spectra. Blanket activity tags can mask spectrum mismatches.

learnings.learning: Every Cure GT has ~6% error rate from NLP extraction. Dominant error: combo product drug mismatch (lidocaine/bupivacaine inheriting corticosteroid indications). 139 rows in source, 82 false GT entries removed. Also found target_overlap rescue was leaking LA procedural demotions back to MEDIUM — same pattern as h560/h647.
learnings.implication: Always check for rescue pathway leakage after implementing demotions. Combo product NLP errors likely affect other drug pairs too. GT quality directly affects holdout evaluation honesty.

learnings.learning: Internal GT (2,999 pairs) is fairly clean for DrugBank-mapped drugs. Main contamination was combo product NLP mismatch (h677, already fixed). FDG PET tracer had 12 false entries but removal has negligible holdout impact. Expanded GT had 1,905 dead-weight broad drug class entries that never matched predictions. GT cleanup is about honesty, not metric improvement.
learnings.implication: Further internal GT cleaning has diminishing returns. Focus future GT work on: (1) expanded GT ID format audit (MESH/CHEBI vs DrugBank matchability), (2) single-drug disease verification, (3) GT gap filling for rare cancers.

learnings.learning: 63% of expanded GT entries are unmatchable by the model (different ID formats or drugs not in internal GT). This doesn't affect precision estimates but means our GT coverage appears much better than it actually is for practical evaluation. The most actionable finding: 149+ internal GT rows lost to simple drug name mismatches between Every Cure and DrugBank naming conventions.
learnings.implication: Drug name aliasing should be a HIGH priority fix — it directly expands the training data with legitimate drug-disease pairs. The 5% internal GT expansion from just 20 aliases suggests there may be many more recoverable entries with broader fuzzy matching.

learnings.learning: Diagnostic imaging agents (Tc-99m sestamibi, Ioflupane, Florbetaben, etc.) are a systematic source of false GT entries in DRKG. They co-occur with diseases in clinical imaging contexts but are NOT therapeutic. 5.3% error rate in single-drug diseases. Iobenguane is DUAL-USE (diagnostic + therapeutic for neuroblastoma/paraganglioma).
learnings.implication: Need systematic census of all diagnostic agents in DRKG (ATC V08/V09). Also check other drug classes that appear in clinical but non-therapeutic contexts.

learnings.learning: Of 64 diagnostic/imaging agents in DrugBank, only ~15 are in DRKG. False GT contamination is concentrated in PET tracers and stimulation test drugs. Pentagastrin had 10 false expanded GT entries including agoraphobia/social anxiety. Comprehensive filter now covers 12 diagnostic agents. Key dual-use exceptions: methylene blue (methemoglobinemia), gallium nitrate (hypercalcemia), I-131 (thyroid), iobenguane (neuroblastoma), metyrapone (Cushing's), tetracosactide (infantile spasms).
learnings.implication: Diagnostic agent contamination is now well-controlled. Future GT additions should be checked against the comprehensive filter list.

learnings.learning: TB drug co-occurrence artifacts are SPECIFIC to isoniazid (3 false entries in h685). Other TB drugs have almost no false associations — most are correctly linked to TB variants or have genuine non-TB uses (streptomycin→plague/tularemia). The isoniazid artifact is driven by its broad prophylactic use in non-TB contexts.
learnings.implication: Co-occurrence artifact risk scales with clinical breadth of use, not drug class. Drugs used prophylactically in non-target diseases are more likely to generate false GT entries.

learnings.learning: 47% of diseases (222/477) have ≤2 internal GT drugs but 8.9x more in expanded GT. This is a structural DRKG extraction limitation, not GT quality. These diseases get poor kNN neighborhoods but represent only 9% of GT entries. Patterns: generic disease names, missing standard treatments (OCD lacks SSRIs, PBC lacks UDCA), outdated single drugs.
learnings.implication: The only way to improve predictions for these 222 diseases is to expand internal GT (h687: add DRKG drugs from expanded GT). Current kNN model cannot compensate for sparse training data.

learnings.learning: Two-drug disease GT error rate = 0% (0/30), much better than single-drug 5.3%. GT error rate decreases with disease drug count. Single-drug diseases are the dominant error source. DrugBank duplicate naming (methylene blue = methylthioninium) can inflate apparent drug count.
learnings.implication: GT quality auditing has diminishing returns beyond single-drug diseases. Focus remaining audit effort on expanded GT or newly added entries.

learnings.learning: Combo product contamination in EC data only affects predictions when the contaminated drug has DRKG edges. The h677 fix (lidocaine/bupivacaine allowlists) was comprehensive — these were the only DRKG drugs with combo product contamination. Non-DRKG substances (edetic acid, zinc oxide, calcium carbonate, chloride ion) had 45 false expanded GT entries but zero prediction impact. EC data contains ~1% non-drug substance rows (excipients, preservatives, allergenic extracts) that don't affect our system.
learnings.implication: No further combo product fixes needed for DRKG drugs. Future GT quality work should focus on DRKG-present drugs only. The expanded GT is now cleaner (57,493 pairs) but this is a data cleanliness improvement, not a prediction improvement.

learnings.learning: CRITICAL: Always use data/raw/drkg/drkg.tsv for DRKG queries, NOT data/drkg/drkg.tsv (which doesn't exist). The h678 analysis was partially incorrect because grep returned 0 by default for the wrong path. Many pharmaceutical excipients/preservatives (chlorobutanol, thimerosal, benzalkonium chloride, etc.) ARE in DRKG with hundreds/thousands of edges, but they don't affect predictions because they're not in EC data (thus not in internal GT). Dual-use substances (edetic acid, zinc oxide, calcium carbonate) need careful handling — they have genuine therapeutic uses alongside excipient roles.
learnings.implication: The expanded GT is now cleaner (57,445 pairs) after removing 48 inert excipient entries. Future DRKG queries must use the correct path. No code changes needed — existing filters handle all impactful cases.

learnings.learning: FDA label "limitations of use" sections cause systematic NLP extraction errors. Oral antidiabetic labels all include "not for T1D or DKA" boilerplate. 37 false EC GT entries found, but none affect DRKG predictions. Main action: sulfonylurea/TZD → T1D inverse indication (7 GOLDEN/HIGH → FILTER).
learnings.implication: NLP-extracted GT databases need drug-class-specific validation. Comp_to_base diabetes hierarchy treats T1D and T2D identically despite fundamentally different pathophysiology.

learnings.learning: Expanded GT for T1D includes 96 drugs from clinical co-occurrence (ClinicalTrials.gov), many not T1D treatments. Sulfonylureas/TZDs are in expanded GT despite being biologically ineffective for T1D. The expanded GT conflates "drug prescribed in T1D context" with "drug treats T1D."
learnings.implication: Disease-specific expanded GT quality varies. For diseases with many comorbidity drugs, expanded GT holdout evaluation is unreliable. Inverse indication filtering is the right tool for medically incorrect predictions rather than hierarchy changes.

learnings.learning: Within ATC coherent infectious: azole antifungals (85%) drive quality, cefuroxime (18%) is weakest. But ATC coherent is holdout-invisible (h653), so class-specific demotion can't be validated. Full-data precision is the only signal.
learnings.implication: ATC coherent quality is drug-class dependent. Antifungals >> antibacterials. But volume too small for actionable drug-level demotions.

learnings.learning: ~3% of EC indicationList rows (31/10224) are false GT from NLP limitation-of-use extraction. Pattern: FDA label says 'Limitations of Use: not indicated for X' and NLP extracts X as indication. 8 drug class patterns identified. None impact predictions because affected drugs/diseases are outside DRKG kNN prediction space. Newer drugs (DPP-4i, SGLT2i, GLP-1 agonists) have DRKG embeddings but generate zero predictions due to insular disease neighborhoods. Removed 5 false GT pairs. Key insight: NLP extraction errors cluster by drug class label templates.
learnings.implication: When extending GT to new drug classes or updating DRKG, check FDA label limitation-of-use sections to avoid importing false indications. Drug classes with standard boilerplate (antidiabetics, ICS, 5-ARIs, biologics) have predictable extraction error patterns.

learnings.learning: Drug coverage gap analysis: 730/1,158 GT drugs (63%) generate predictions. 41.3% of GT drugs are invisible (never predicted for any disease). Critical mass: GT≥3 diseases → 83.6% prediction rate; GT=1 → 31.8%. Biologics (54 drugs), newer antihypertensives (20), newer antidiabetics (10) are the largest invisible classes. 28 diseases generate zero predictions. Corticosteroids dominate: top 9 of 20 most-predicted drugs, prednisolone→143 diseases.
learnings.implication: GT expansion for single-indication drugs is the highest-ROI improvement possible: adding just 1 indication to GT=1 drugs doubles prediction rate (31.8%→59.1%). Biologics and newer drug classes need GT expansion to become visible to kNN. Consider alternative methods (ATC transfer, gene overlap) for 28 zero-prediction diseases.

learnings.learning: 28 zero-prediction diseases: 24 absent from DRKG (newer MESH terms), 4 have correct predictions incorrectly filtered. Anti-VEGF drugs for retinal diseases (PDR, ROP) are the highest-impact rescue. Parent disease transfer works for 5/9 subtypes (HoFH best at 100% GT capture).
learnings.implication: DRKG disease coverage has a systematic gap for post-2016 MESH terms. Filter rules can create false negatives for niche but correct predictions. Parent disease fallback mechanism could rescue ~8 diseases.

learnings.learning: Anti-VEGF drugs (ranibizumab, aflibercept) have tiny GT footprint (2-3 diseases), causing freq<=2 in kNN. The COMPLICATION_VALIDATED_DRUGS list already included them but the freq filter was applied BEFORE the complication check. Moving the complication bypass upstream rescued 3 correct predictions without holdout regression.
learnings.implication: The freq<=2 filter is a blunt instrument. Drugs with legitimate but narrow indications (anti-VEGF, orphan drugs) may be systematically penalized. The validated complication bypass is a principled way to rescue known-good drugs.

learnings.learning: Benign/intermediate proliferative disorders (hemangioendothelioma, LAM, lymphangioma) are categorized as cancer but not recognized as cancer types by extract_cancer_types(). This caused their GT drug (sirolimus) to be incorrectly filtered by cancer_no_gt. Adding a new 'vascular_proliferative' cancer type resolved the issue.
learnings.implication: When adding diseases to the cancer category keyword list, always verify that extract_cancer_types() also recognizes them. Cancer category + unrecognized cancer type = systematic false FILTER.

learnings.learning: DPP-4i and GLP-1 drugs don't appear in pancreatitis predictions despite having DRKG embeddings — their kNN neighborhoods are diabetes-centric, not GI-centric. Only 1 pancreatitis-causing drug (azathioprine) was predicted for chronic pancreatitis. Corticosteroids and everolimus were already handled by prior inverse indication work.
learnings.implication: Drug-induced pancreatitis is well-covered by existing inverse indications (h476/h486) plus the azathioprine addition. kNN self-selects against most problematic drug-disease pairs because they inhabit different embedding neighborhoods.

learnings.learning: DRKG disease coverage is 95.2% (453/476 predictor diseases have embeddings). The real data gap is disease NAME MATCHING: DiseaseMatcher maps only 43.1% of EC disease names (1159/2688). This loses 50.9% of EC drug-disease pairs. Most failures are simple synonyms (migraine, emphysema, nausea, depression) that have MESH IDs in DRKG but aren't in the matcher. Better matching could double internal GT.
learnings.implication: h407 (Comprehensive ID Mapping) and h712 (Synonym Expansion) are highest-ROI. DRKG updating is NOT a priority.

learnings.learning: ICS/controller → acute respiratory condition safety concern does not exist: acute conditions (status asthmaticus, bronchospasm) lack DRKG embeddings. Controller drugs are overwhelmingly predicted for chronic conditions where they're appropriate. However, IPF has 67% antihistamine predictions due to kNN embedding near allergic disease neighborhood — a new drug-class/disease-subtype mismatch pattern.
learnings.implication: Respiratory disease subtypes (obstructive/allergic/fibrotic) may need subtype-specific drug class filters, similar to antimicrobial-pathogen mismatch (h560). IPF antihistamine issue is a concrete example.

learnings.learning: The +55.6pp expanded GT lift for infectious_cs_tb is explained by 54 CS-infectious pairs across 25 diseases. Most are legitimate (WHO TB guidelines, Surviving Sepsis Campaign, de Gans meningitis trial). CS + chronic HBV is a historical practice now considered dangerous. Autoimmune hepatitis despite its name is correctly treated with CS (first-line therapy).
learnings.implication: CS adjunctive therapy for infections is a well-established medical practice. The internal GT is simply incomplete for this pattern. No action needed — the expanded GT correctly captures clinical practice.

learnings.learning: Internal GT frequency is NOT the binding constraint on MEDIUM tier size. 2x GT would only add 50-90 MEDIUM predictions (3-6%). The real bottlenecks are: (1) mechanism support (77% of eligible LOW lack it), (2) category-specific demotions (51%), (3) rank quality (only R1-5 match MEDIUM). Cancer targeted therapy at LOW has surprising 34% GT hit rate.
learnings.implication: Pursuing more internal GT has diminishing returns. Focus should be on mechanism path coverage in DRKG and re-evaluating category-specific demotion thresholds.

learnings.learning: 2-hop mechanism paths through DRKG gene-gene network do NOT predict treatment efficacy. Network too dense (27K genes, 2.35M edges) — at 2 hops, specificity collapses. Holdout: 2hop>=4 = 25.5% vs no-2hop = 23.2% (p>0.5). Direct 1-hop overlap remains the only valid mechanism signal.
learnings.implication: Do NOT attempt mechanism path expansion. Focus on improving direct gene coverage: (a) supplement gene-poor diseases with external databases, (b) category-specific mechanism may work for psychiatric/dermatological.

learnings.learning: Gene-disease databases have a fundamental specificity tradeoff: curated (CTD direct) gives 0-7 genes per infectious disease (too sparse for mechanism overlap), while inferred (CTD all) gives 6K-23K genes (60-85% of drugs overlap = noise). Infectious diseases lack human genetic etiology — gene-based mechanism checks are structurally inappropriate for them. Need alternative mechanism proxy (antimicrobial spectrum matching).
learnings.implication: For infectious diseases, drug antimicrobial spectrum matching pathogen type is the biologically appropriate mechanism substitute. Also check gene-sparse (not zero) diseases where supplementary genes may help.

learnings.learning: Antimicrobial spectrum matching (correct drug class for pathogen type) has 35.1% full-data precision but only 29.2% ± 14.7% holdout — NOT significantly different from non-antimicrobial LOW (31.0%). Full-data→holdout gap driven by R11-20 dominance. Spectrum matching is correctly used for demotion (h560, 0% mismatch) but the positive signal is too weak for promotion. Infectious diseases are inherently hard for holdout: small GT footprint + few diseases in holdout per seed.
learnings.implication: CLOSED: Antimicrobial spectrum matching for tier promotion. The asymmetry (demotion works, promotion doesn't) is because mismatches are clean biological impossibilities (0%), while matches are necessary but not sufficient (antimicrobial must also be clinically appropriate for the specific pathogen).

learnings.learning: Cancer targeted therapy has the largest full-data-to-holdout inflation ratio in the tier system (5.9x). Full-data=36.0%, holdout=6.1%. Even R1-5+mech: 19.3% ± 16.6% (tiny n=10.6/seed). The h598 demotion is biologically correct: targeted therapies target specific biomarkers that are cancer-subtype-specific. kNN transfers drug recommendations based on disease similarity, but biomarker profiles (BRAF V600E, HER2+) don't correlate with disease embedding similarity.
learnings.implication: Full-data precision is deeply misleading for biomarker-dependent drugs. Future targeted therapy improvements require biomarker-matching (DRKG mutation edges), not kNN-based signals. Checkpoint inhibitors may transfer better than kinase inhibitors (pan-cancer approvals).

learnings.learning: Even pan-cancer immunotherapy (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) doesn't transfer via kNN to holdout cancers. Checkpoint=10.1%, Kinase=5.9%, mAb=2.7%, PARP=0%. This confirms targeted therapy demotion is biologically correct across ALL sub-classes. Biomarker profiles (MSI-high, TMB-high, PD-L1, BRCA) are not captured in DRKG disease embeddings. Full-data inflation is 2-4x for all sub-classes.
learnings.implication: CLOSED: No targeted therapy sub-class rescue is possible via kNN. Biomarker-matching (h728) is the only remaining path for targeted therapy improvement.

learnings.learning: Drug name aliasing recovered 85 GT pairs from 34 aliases. Key patterns: INN variants (US vs international: albuterol/salbutamol, meperidine/pethidine), salt form differences beyond suffix stripping (fondaparinux/fondaparinux sodium), 'only product' suffix (inotuzumab ozogamicin only product), combo product→primary drug (piperacillin-tazobactam→piperacillin is safe when both drugs share indications, unlike h677 lidocaine/hydrocortisone). Biologic variants (epoetin alfa/beta/zeta all map to erythropoietin). MEDIUM holdout improved 38.3→42.8% with std dropping 4.7→1.8%.
learnings.implication: Drug name aliasing is a high-ROI activity. 787 EC drugs still unmapped, but remaining ones are mostly combo products, vaccines, and newer drugs not in DrugBank. Future work: systematic combo product drug mapping (h686 extension).

learnings.learning: Literature evidence (ClinicalTrials.gov + PubMed) is a strong independent predictor of holdout precision. STRONG_EVIDENCE = 78.7% holdout (above HIGH 57.6%). MEDIUM+STRONG = 67.4% (HIGH quality). Score quartile gradient: Q1=82.5%, Q2=56.7%, Q3=16.9%, Q4=19.5%. Found 31 genuine GT gaps and 1 inverse indication from 590 predictions mined.
learnings.implication: Literature mining should be extended to all predictions for evidence-based tier adjustments. MEDIUM+STRONG evidence is a clear promotion candidate.

learnings.learning: MEDIUM known=97.0% (n=483) vs novel=29.5% (n=850). 42.8% average is 57% driven by known indications. Literature NO_EVIDENCE (16.0%) ≈ novel NOT_ASSESSED baseline within same tier rules. STRONG_EVIDENCE (67.8%) is the actionable signal, not NO_EVIDENCE. Novel sub-rule variation: target_overlap/cancer_same_type/atc_coherent/freq5_mech (40-50%) vs default_nomech (16-20%) vs LA (7.3%).
learnings.implication: Cannot demote NO_EVIDENCE (biased sample). Should promote STRONG_EVIDENCE (h732) and report known vs novel precision separately (h738). Deliverable is stale (h736).

learnings.learning: Known-indication inflation is massive across ALL tiers. Novel tier precision: GOLDEN 53.4%, HIGH 33.1%, MEDIUM 21.5%, LOW 7.3%, FILTER 6.2%. The tier system IS valid for novel predictions (ordering preserved) but reported precisions are 2-4x inflated by known-indication contamination. MEDIUM 47.0% → 21.5% novel.
learnings.implication: Must report novel precision alongside total precision in deliverables. Sub-rule analysis identifies highly_repurposable (4.5%) and default_nomech (15-18%) as below-MEDIUM quality for novel predictions.

learnings.learning: Removing low-quality MEDIUM predictions that include known indications will DECREASE overall MEDIUM precision (because known indications have ~80% holdout) but INCREASE novel MEDIUM precision. Novel precision is the correct optimization target for drug repurposing since known indications are not actionable.
learnings.implication: Always report novel precision when evaluating demotion impact. Overall precision is misleading due to known-indication inflation.

learnings.learning: kNN score is a strong GT-free quality predictor within MEDIUM nomech predictions. Score < 2.0 has 7.7% holdout (vs 30+% above 2.0). Novel predictions are 4x more likely to be low-score (36.3% vs 8.5%). Adding knn_score to _assign_confidence_tier enabled the first score-based demotion rule.
learnings.implication: kNN score may be useful across OTHER sub-rules too, not just nomech. Could extend to freq5_mechanism, target_overlap, etc.

learnings.learning: Epilepsy and gout hierarchy GOLDEN rules were 4-5x overfitted (58%/37.5% full-data vs 12%/16% holdout). Demoting to MEDIUM improved GOLDEN by +7.8pp with minimal MEDIUM dilution (-0.4pp). Full h393 revalidation also reveals current absolute tier values differ from CLAUDE.md due to h744-h746 intermediate changes.
learnings.implication: Hierarchy rules for small disease groups (<100 preds) are especially prone to overfitting. Always validate new hierarchy rules with holdout before deploying. Current tier holdout: GOLDEN 78.0%, HIGH 56.8%, MEDIUM 35.5%.

learnings.learning: GI HIGH holdout 69.9% ± 16.8% — above HIGH avg but below GOLDEN. h749's 90.4% was from smaller subsample. n=11.4/seed is too sparse for reliable per-category promotion decisions.
learnings.implication: Per-category GOLDEN promotions need n>30/seed minimum. GI has only 43 diseases total (8-9 holdout/seed). Focus on improving existing HIGH rules rather than promoting sparse categories.

learnings.learning: Category-specific 2-hop mechanism: full-data to holdout inflation is ~2x (psychiatric 52.8% → 22.7%, dermatological 37.8% → 25.0%). No category reaches MEDIUM threshold. The DRKG gene-gene network's density destroys 2-hop specificity even within categories.
learnings.implication: 2-hop mechanism is CLOSED as a path to MEDIUM tier expansion, regardless of category filtering. Mechanism expansion requires better gene-disease data (DisGeNET/OMIM), not longer paths.

learnings.learning: Comprehensive sub-reason audit improved all tiers: GOLDEN +9.2pp, HIGH +5.7pp, MEDIUM +2.6pp. Key pattern: rules originally set from full-data precision (h183 reproductive hormones 26.3% → HIGH, h265 fluoroquinolones 44.4% → HIGH) are severely overfitted — holdout drops to 8-29%. All category-specific HIGH rules should be holdout-validated. freq10_nomech_r6_10 (high-frequency drugs without mechanism at rank 6-10) is genuinely LOW quality — frequency alone without mechanism or top-5 rank doesn't indicate repurposability.
learnings.implication: Remaining MEDIUM watch candidates: target_overlap_promotion (35.2%), cancer_same_type variants (~39%). These are borderline and may need deeper sub-analysis. Also: many hierarchy rules are holdout-invisible (0 n/seed) — they can't be validated but may still provide value.

learnings.learning: Hierarchy rule audit: 10/32 rules are holdout-invisible (n=0/seed). diabetes MEDIUM→LOW (+1.1pp MEDIUM) and copd HIGH→MEDIUM. Invisible rules affect ~78 predictions but are medically reasonable. Full-data precision is DEEPLY misleading for hierarchy rules (62.8pp gap for diabetes).
learnings.implication: Full-data precision for hierarchy rules should never be trusted. All tier assignments need holdout validation. Rules with <4 GT diseases are evaluation blind spots.

learnings.learning: Literature mining validates all 8 holdout-invisible HIGH hierarchy rules (82% STRONG evidence). No demotions needed. PubMed exact-match search fails for very specific disease names (0/6 for CF pseudomonas, 0/2 for ATTR cardiomyopathy) — all false negatives confirmed by manual review.
learnings.implication: Literature mining is a reliable independent validation signal for holdout-invisible rules. Pipeline needs disease name simplification for specific/rare conditions.

learnings.learning: Hierarchy predictions have systematic GT gaps for well-known treatments. 166 gaps found across 44 diseases. Most common: sepsis antibiotics (10), emphysema drugs (10), cellulitis antibiotics (7), seizure drugs (10), dyslipidemia statins (8). Adding 49 conservative FDA-approved pairs improved MEDIUM +1.7pp. Remaining 117 gaps need literature validation.
learnings.implication: GT expansion from hierarchy predictions is a reliable, low-risk way to improve evaluation accuracy. Literature mining should be applied systematically to all holdout-invisible predictions.

learnings.learning: Literature mining STRONG evidence for GT gaps has ~100% false positive rate when existing GT is comprehensive. 7/14 STRONG gaps were inverse indications (drug CAUSES the condition). Literature co-mention ≠ therapeutic indication. Always validate STRONG hits against known drug mechanisms.
learnings.implication: GT gap mining is approaching diminishing returns for GOLDEN/HIGH non-hierarchy predictions. Future GT expansion should focus on specific drug classes or disease categories with known incompleteness.

learnings.learning: Literature STRONG rate correlates with MEDIUM sub-reason quality: comp_to_base_high_87 (100%), respiratory_hierarchy_copd (69%), cancer_same_type_high_rank (58%) vs hematological (0%), atc_coherent_infectious (14%). Sub-reasons with 0% STRONG evidence are CS-artifact driven.
learnings.implication: Literature evidence rate can serve as external validation signal for sub-reason quality, independent of holdout precision.

learnings.learning: Class-level inverse indication expansion has diminishing returns — most drug-disease pairs are already caught by other filters (cross_domain_isolated, category demotion, etc.). The main value is safety/defensive coverage. Propranolol→hypotension was the only MEDIUM-tier catch. Diuretics→hyponatremia discovered as new inverse indication class (spironolactone→hyponatremia [MEDIUM]).
learnings.implication: Focus inverse indication work on MEDIUM-tier predictions only — LOW/FILTER are already caught. Diuretic inverse indications (h775) are the highest-value next step.

learnings.learning: Inverse indication class expansion (ACEi→angioedema, aminoglycosides→nephrotoxicity) is low-impact since most class members do not generate relevant predictions. Only 2 predictions moved. Defensive entries still valuable for safety.
learnings.implication: Future inverse indication expansions should check actual prediction counts BEFORE implementation to assess whether effort is justified.

learnings.learning: Systematic inverse indication audit shows 6/13 drug classes have incomplete class coverage, but ZERO actual predictions need filtering. kNN does not generate predictions for drugs→diseases they cause (the embeddings naturally separate them). Inverse indications are mostly defensive entries.
learnings.implication: Future inverse indication work has diminishing returns. Only add entries when actual predictions are found (check predictions FIRST, then add entries). The kNN embedding space already separates most harmful drug-disease pairs.

learnings.learning: 32.6% of diseases never appear in holdout across 5 seeds (theoretical: 32.8%). GOLDEN is most inflated (+7.8pp) because 53.9% of GOLDEN preds come from never-holdout high-GT diseases (RA, hypertension, UC). MEDIUM inflation +8.2pp. Tier ordering perfectly preserved in visible-only analysis. Using 15+ seeds would reduce never-holdout to <3.5%.
learnings.implication: Full-data precision overestimates by ~8pp for GOLDEN/MEDIUM. Not actionable for tier design (ordering preserved). Could use more seeds for calibration.

learnings.learning: DRKG disease names cause 33.8% (285/842) of NO_EVIDENCE false negatives via: concatenated words (stevensjohnson), pathogen qualifiers (caused by X), excessive specificity (>55 chars). Disease name simplification with known overrides + automated rules rescues 53% of testable pairs. Key patterns: pathogen-first ordering for "caused by" qualifiers, adjectival pathogen expansion (gonococcal→gonorrhea), and embedded abbreviation removal.
learnings.implication: Future literature mining runs will automatically use fallback names. Re-run on all NO_EVIDENCE pairs to populate evidence. Approximately 151 pairs can be rescued.

learnings.learning: Disease name simplification rescues 61% of NO_EVIDENCE pairs (174/285). Key patterns: ADHD from verbose clinical descriptions, pseudomonas from pathogen-specific names, lymphoma subtypes. Broad simplification can inflate PubMed counts (meningococcal→general meningitis). Primary value is annotation improvement for deliverable.
learnings.implication: Literature mining coverage can be improved further with alternative simplification strategies for the remaining 557 pairs.

learnings.learning: Literature evidence_score is the strongest independent predictor of holdout precision, creating 60-70pp gradients within every tier. LOW+score6-9=81% exceeds HIGH overall=73%. FILTER+score6-9=90% exceeds GOLDEN=80%. Coverage is the bottleneck: MEDIUM only 19% cached, HIGH 62% cached.
learnings.implication: Prioritize evidence-based tier overrides (h789) and MEDIUM coverage expansion (h790). Evidence score should be primary deliverable sorting criterion within tiers.

learnings.learning: Literature evidence tier override validated across ALL tiers. STRONG LOW/FILTER→HIGH: 76.9% holdout (n=87). HIGH NO/WEAK→MEDIUM: 31.4% (n=28). Combined: HIGH +3.9pp (74.0→77.9%). Literature evidence is now the strongest single signal for tier mobility in both directions.
learnings.implication: Expanding literature cache coverage is highest-ROI next step. Current 3115 entries only cover ~19% of MEDIUM. Full coverage could double tier movements. Evidence-based tier overrides should be applied LAST in the tier assignment pipeline (after all rule-based assignments).

learnings.learning: Literature mining cache is nearly complete for actionable tiers (GOLDEN 69%, HIGH 99.6%, MEDIUM 98.5%). LOW/FILTER mining has 0% STRONG rate across all sub-reasons (n=1,056 cached). Mining 17,826 uncached LOW/FILTER predictions would yield near-zero tier promotions. Future literature work should focus on GOLDEN validation (478 predictions) and GT gap expansion, not broad LOW/FILTER mining.
learnings.implication: Literature mining has hit diminishing returns for tier mobility. Pivot to: (1) GOLDEN validation, (2) GT gap expansion, (3) non-literature signals for LOW rescue.

learnings.learning: Cancer same-type full-data inflation is 15.9pp (85.4%→69.5%) even for mech+rank≤10 subset. 'Other' category literature_strong_low has only 39% holdout (vs 85.7% non-other). Disease GT richness (24% for GT≥50 vs 3% for GT≤4) is strongest LOW-internal signal but cannot promote safely due to mix of correctly-demoted sub-reasons.
learnings.implication: Never trust full-data cancer precision. Disease GT count is strong quality proxy but cannot be used alone for tier promotion. 'Other' category should be excluded from any evidence-based promotion rules.

learnings.learning: WEAK_EVIDENCE and NO_EVIDENCE have identical holdout precision (29.1% vs 29.3%) for literature_high_demotion predictions. The categorical distinction between no evidence and weak evidence provides zero predictive value for this tier system. Also discovered MODERATE_EVIDENCE (550 entries) is unhandled by production_predictor.py.
learnings.implication: Current demotion is appropriately calibrated. MODERATE_EVIDENCE is a potential improvement opportunity (h806). Sub-reason analysis of what HIGH rules are being demoted may reveal protected rules (h808).

learnings.learning: MODERATE_EVIDENCE correctly handled as NOT_ASSESSED — HIGH+MOD=63.2% (stays HIGH), MEDIUM+MOD=40.6% (stays MEDIUM), LOW+MOD=33.2% (borderline, stays LOW). Literature evidence has clean monotonic gradient in LOW tier: STRONG 43.7% > MODERATE 33.2% > WEAK 19.1% > NO 9.3% ≈ NOT_ASSESSED 10.8%.
learnings.implication: No code changes. Literature evidence level is the best sub-tier discriminator within LOW. Consider continuous evidence score for finer granularity (h807).

learnings.learning: Literature-demoted HIGH predictions are NOT uniform quality. Only default_freq10_nomech_r1_5 (36.4%) maintains MEDIUM quality. All other sub-reasons (cancer_same_type_mech_rank10: 13.4%, default: 15.7%) are LOW quality when literature evidence is weak. Double-demotion freed +1.5pp MEDIUM.
learnings.implication: Blanket protection rules should be audited for sub-group heterogeneity. Composite rules (like literature × original-tier) may mask quality differences.

learnings.learning: RA hierarchy dropped from 86.4% (h615) to 69.0% (current) holdout due to GT/rule changes reducing RA prediction count (23→16/seed). Seed 42 had 0 RA preds in holdout. Extreme per-seed variance (22-100%) flags small-n instability. Hierarchy rules with <20 preds/seed are unreliable — always check per-seed breakdown before trusting aggregate.
learnings.implication: Audit all hierarchy GOLDEN promotions for n<20/seed instability. Consider minimum n threshold for GOLDEN eligibility.

learnings.learning: WEAK_EVIDENCE predictions (34.1% holdout) are MEDIUM-range but below the post-h815 MEDIUM average (38.5%). Blanket WEAK rescue dilutes MEDIUM by -2.0pp. However, per-sub-reason analysis reveals heterogeneity: some WEAK sub-reasons (default_no_mech_high_rank 39.8%, default_freq10_nomech_r6_10 52.6%) are above MEDIUM while others (nomech_r1_5_low_score 11.4%) are below.
learnings.implication: When evaluating tier changes, always check against current tier averages (not historical). Per-sub-reason rescue may succeed where blanket rescue fails (h818).

learnings.learning: CS SOC revert (h814) + MODERATE LOW promotion (h815) combined for HIGH +2.1pp and MEDIUM +2.2pp. These were independently implemented but their effects compound: CS predictions dropping from HIGH to MEDIUM absorbed into the MODERATE-boosted MEDIUM pool.
learnings.implication: Track cumulative tier state, not just individual hypothesis deltas. Compounding effects between hypotheses can be significant.

learnings.learning: h901 MeSH mapping expansion (917->1555, +70%) yielded only +7.2% evaluable diseases (965->1034) and 0 new GOLDEN predictions. 54% of new mappings were symptoms/findings/clinical qualifiers that should not generate treatment predictions (agitation, vomiting, back pain). Mapping expansion is at diminishing returns; the real bottleneck is DRKG embedding coverage for rare diseases, not disease-name normalization.
learnings.implication: Pivot research loop to external data hypotheses (h905 LINCS, h906 DrugBank, h907 Ryland). Mapping expansion is CLOSED. Audit h901 additions for symptom/finding leakage (h908). Establish predicted-coverage scoring so future mapping rounds are targeted, not blind (h910).

learnings.learning: The h901 mapping expansion did NOT hit an external-data bottleneck. All 638 new mappings have DRKG embeddings; 626/638 have GT drugs. The 569 'missing evaluable' are blocked INSIDE the pipeline (symptoms 54%, holdout sampling, name-resolution). External data (LINCS, DrugBank) gives <60 new evaluable diseases across the full 1,555 — it cannot be justified as a coverage pivot.
learnings.implication: Reframe h905/h906 as PRECISION pivots (biologics, rare-disease features) not coverage pivots. Prioritize h907 (Ryland blinded labels) and pipeline-hygiene hypotheses (h908 symptom filter, new h910 below) over external data coverage.

learnings.learning: h900 mechanism-only fallback never fires (0/1034 full-data, 0/207 seed-42 holdout). self.train_diseases are pre-filtered to require GT+embeddings, so drug_scores is always populated from kNN neighbors. If forced to run, fallback precision is 5.96% (below FILTER 9.2%).
learnings.implication: Remove h900 fallback (75 lines, production_predictor.py:4634-4709). Do NOT extend it; target-overlap ranking alone is a weak repurposing signal. Future rare-disease coverage work should increase the population of train_diseases (GT expansion for evaluable rare diseases), not add a parallel ranking path.

learnings.learning: Target-overlap ranking (|drug_targets ∩ disease_genes|) is NOT a valid standalone repurposing signal. Per-disease mean R@30 = 3.47% across 2,253 evaluable diseases, vs kNN 17.95% on same. No covariate (gene-set size, max overlap, category, GT size, in-train, kNN strength) isolates a subpopulation above 15% R@30 at n>=30. Cancer is the only category >10% (11.89%) and reveals a complementary niche: 11/104 cancer diseases where target > kNN (target mean 25.32% vs kNN 11.22% on those).
learnings.implication: (1) h900 mechanism-only fallback is permanently invalidated as a tier. (2) MinRank fusion (_minrank_fusion at production_predictor.py:3327) deserves one more test on cancer diseases with weak kNN (h914). (3) If cancer fusion fails, remove all target-overlap-only infrastructure including h900 fallback + helpers (h915). (4) The cancer-only signal likely reflects drug-target database density, not biology (h916) — informs h906 DrugBank scoping.

learnings.learning: Expert-label ingestion is independent infrastructure: schema + importer + leakage-safe loader + parallel precision evaluator. The whole scaffold was buildable BEFORE the review arrived. Key design choice: expert labels live in their own file (data/reference/expert_labels_ryland.json) with provenance tag, never merged into predictor.ground_truth. This preserves the evaluation independence that makes external labels valuable in the first place.
learnings.implication: Future external-label sources (clinician reviews, RCT-curated pairs, etc.) should follow the same provenance-tagged parallel-precision pattern. Do NOT push external labels into expanded_ground_truth; it kills their evaluative independence.

learnings.learning: MeSH tree-class classification (C23 symptom vs C01-C99 disease) gives a precise 8.2% non-disease share of h901 mappings, vs h902's 54% keyword-only estimate. Symptom-level MeSH IDs inherit poor kNN neighborhoods and generate antibiotic/NSAID-to-symptom artifacts in MEDIUM tier. Curated blocklist of 45 names removes 300 deliverable rows without tier-precision regression.
learnings.implication: For any future disease-mapping expansion, classify by MeSH tree node (not keyword) and exclude C23-only entries. Also audit pre-existing hardcoded mappings (h926) and remap symptom-level kept names to disorder-level IDs (h925).

learnings.learning: Dead h900 mechanism-only fallback removed (~75 lines) — self.train_diseases pre-filter on GT+embeddings makes the if-not-drug_scores branch unreachable. Verified by h903; this session executed the cleanup.
learnings.implication: Other rescue/fallback paths in production_predictor.py may be similarly unreachable. h935 proposes a coverage-driven sweep.

learnings.learning: Cancer's target-overlap concentration (target_r30 0.119 vs 0.032 baseline) is NOT a drug-target-density artifact (r=0.136, ns) but also not a generalizable gene-set-size signal (cross-cat r=0.868 collapses to 0.353 without cancer; within-cat r near zero). Cancer's max_overlap is 28.5 vs 2.6 baseline — >10x — because cancer drugs and cancer diseases share a common cancer-gene vocabulary (oncogenes/TSGs/kinases). Target-overlap is a cancer-semantic signal, not a density feature. This invalidates the h916 null hypothesis but also weakens h906's assumed general applicability.
learnings.implication: DrugBank integration (h906) needs more granular features than raw target-overlap: target family, pathway membership, or biologic-specific target specificity. A blanket 'target overlap' feature will replicate h912's category concentration. Priority pivot: h939 (biologic-only target_r30) to confirm or deny h906's premise before investing effort.

learnings.learning: Target-overlap is a biologic signal (3-11x SM ratio across 4 categories; 26.5% bio_r30 vs 5.5% SM). Polypharmacy dilutes SM overlap but mAbs/fusions have clean 1:1 target mapping. h906 motivation preserved but precision is similar - deploy as fusion feature, not replacement.
learnings.implication: Pursue h940 (biologic-only target+kNN fusion) ahead of full h906 DrugBank integration. h921 (ESM2 target embeddings) becomes more attractive because target-similarity > binary overlap for the 266-drug biologic pool. Deprioritize h906 until h940 quantifies achievable biologic R@30 gain.

learnings.learning: Biologic target-overlap is NOT additive to kNN when biologics compete against small molecules. h939's 3-11x biologic/SM ratio held only within the biologic-only 266-drug pool. In a mixed ranking, kNN transfer learning is strictly stronger for biologic R@30 (31.4% baseline vs 22-27% under any fusion alpha). Target-overlap should be used as an annotation/audit signal, not a re-ranker.
learnings.implication: Reframe h906 motivation away from 'fix biologic recall via target features.' Remaining viable biologic-signal uses: (a) precision-side demotion rules for biologic predictions with zero disease-gene overlap; (b) h921 ESM2 protein embeddings as a DEEPER target signal; (c) fusion by annotation (feature in meta-confidence model) rather than re-ranking.

learnings.learning: The biologic-failure narrative driving h906/h920/h921/h924 is FALSE on the current production pipeline. 5-seed apples-to-apples holdout: bio_r30 = 27.06% +/- 3.12% vs overall_r30 = 16.39% +/- 1.10%. Biologics OUTPERFORM overall by +10.67pp. The historical 27.3% biologic R@30 was numerically correct (we measured 27.06%) but it was being compared to a 41.8% overall number from a different evaluation framework that no longer reflects honest holdout performance. Bio precision is the genuine remaining gap (bio_p30 = 6.37%); recall is fine. Per-category bio:sm ratios where biologics dominate: gastrointestinal 7.9x, hematological 7.4x, metabolic 3.8x, neurological 3.2x, musculoskeletal 3.0x.
learnings.implication: Close or re-justify h906/h920/h921/h924 (h955). Pivot any biologic work from RECALL to PRECISION (h953). Diagnose the production-vs-plain-kNN regression of -4.36pp bio_r30 / -3.91pp overall_r30 (h952) — likely SELECTIVE category boost or tier safety filters demoting correct predictions. Fix the documented 41.8% baseline that is misleading every hypothesis rationale (h954). Generic lesson: motivation baselines decay silently; require rationale-baselines to be re-measured on the current framework before greenlighting external-data efforts.

learnings.learning: Walked h906/h920/h921/h924 rationales after h951's MOTIVATION DISSOLVED finding. All four moved to status=inconclusive. h920/h921/h924 demoted P2->P3. Re-justification attempts failed: h906 (no remaining recall path; h949 covers the only precision use); h920 (text-precision pivot is plausible but unvalidated, gated on h956 CPU smoke test); h921 (h940 pool-fusion failure mode is granularity-independent, ESM2 won't fix it); h924 (LINCS is small-molecule-biased, biologic precision use is moot). Net effect: ~1 month of GPU/license effort freed for h952/h953/h954/h957.
learnings.implication: Generic lesson: when a motivating baseline is dissolved, the dependent hypotheses rarely have a clean alternative motivation — most close cleanly. Always interrogate dependent hypotheses immediately when a motivating finding lands; do not let them sit in pending limbo. Three new actionable hypotheses generated: h956 (PubMedBERT CPU smoke test, low-cost precision-impact estimate), h957 (h949 zero-overlap biologic safety filter, in-pipeline precision pivot).

learnings.learning: The h940 plain-kNN vs h951 production recall gap (~4pp) was entirely a find_disease_id name-resolution bug, not a methodology or SELECTIVE_BOOST issue. Adding a reverse-index fallback (disease_names lowercased -> disease_id) restores overall_r30 to plain-kNN parity (18.72% vs 18.71% at seed 42) and actually pushes bio_r30 slightly above plain kNN (31.96% vs 30.17%). 58% of disease_names entries were missing from mesh_mappings.
learnings.implication: Any past experiment that used predictor.predict(disease_name_from_disease_names) silently dropped ~20% of holdout diseases. Historical baselines (h951 bio_r30 27.06%, h904 tier precisions, many per-category deltas) need re-verification against the fixed predictor. The biologic-failure dissolution (h951) is strengthened, not weakened, by the fix.

learnings.learning: The h952 find_disease_id bug suppressed recall for 21.1% of holdout diseases in h393 (213/1011). Deliverable NOT affected (uses disease_id path). h939/h940 custom kNN NOT affected. h904/h908/h951 directionally valid but magnitudes dampened. 111 of 112 callers pass disease_name — only h771 passes id and was actually broken (find_disease_id can't resolve ids).
learnings.implication: Downstream corrections: (1) add ID fast-path to predict() to eliminate class of bugs, (2) regression test for silent-zero outputs, (3) re-run h904/h908 tier precisions post-fix to update CLAUDE.md magnitudes.

learnings.learning: Baseline drift was a micro-vs-macro R@30 + GT-version pitfall: 41.8% is micro-averaged pool recall on Every-Cure-only GT (442 diseases) via a GB classifier; 19.49% is macro-averaged per-disease R@30 on expanded GT (1011 diseases) via kNN+tier production_predictor. Zero pending hypotheses cite 41.8% — drift contained to top-level docs.
learnings.implication: Document micro-vs-macro explicitly whenever quoting R@30. research_spec.md and initializer_prompt.md updated; a CLAUDE.md metric-hygiene subsection proposed (h967).

learnings.learning: Zero-overlap biologic safety filter: precision lift +3.22pp confirms target-engagement is a real biologic-correctness signal, but global deployment costs -15.54pp bio_r30. Per-category split: cancer (+2.6/-2.1) and musculoskeletal (+26/0) work; autoimmune/neurological/respiratory fail catastrophically because disease_genes does not capture cytokine-signaling targets that anti-cytokine biologics bind. Filter is mechanism-aware in oncology (TCGA-dense), mechanism-blind in inflammatory disease.
learnings.implication: Apply target-overlap filtering only to categories where disease_genes captures the actual MoA target space (cancer first). For inflammatory categories, need pathway-membership overlap (h966) before filter is safe. Do not deploy global form.

learnings.learning: Cancer-restricted zero-overlap biologic filter: cancer-cohort signal +2.54pp p30 / -2.24pp r30 reproduces h957's cancer slice exactly, but cancer is only ~12% of evaluable diseases so the global tier-rule impact dilutes to +0.28pp p30 / -0.46pp r30 — below shipping threshold. Non-cancer cohort Δ=0.00pp everywhere confirms clean filter isolation.
learnings.implication: The biologic-overlap signal is too narrow at the disease-category level to ship as a single tier rule. Right surface area is per-prediction annotation (h968) or subclass-level rule on canonical anti-target biologics (h969).

learnings.learning: h173 neurological supplement is benign for R@30: the early-return at `if not missing_drugs` fires for all holdout neuro diseases because kNN top-30 already contains the class-matched drugs the supplement would inject. h952's -2.85pp boost+supp neuro regression therefore CANNOT be blamed on the supplement; the search shifts to SELECTIVE_BOOST itself (h972).
learnings.implication: When investigating production-vs-baseline regressions on a stratum, ablate each pipeline component independently — don't assume the named feature is the cause without measuring. The supplement's name suggested it was active but its early-return short-circuit makes it inert on the very stratum that motivated it (h171's coverage gap was on FULL data, not on holdout).

learnings.learning: Post-h952-fix tier precisions drifted >1pp across all 5 tiers; GOLDEN std widened 4.6x (1.3→6.0) due to newly-resolving diseases contributing seed-dependent hits.
learnings.implication: h904/h908 decisions are still valid (relative Δ within same framework) but CLAUDE.md absolute tier numbers needed correction. Tier ordering is preserved within noise; GOLDEN/HIGH overlap requires 10-seed resolution (filed as follow-up).

learnings.learning: h952 bug-fix changed per-rule status for 30 of 80 tier rules. 3 actionable candidates emerge: infectious_hierarchy_uti rescue (h904 may have over-demoted), immunological_medium_demotion LOW→FILTER, cancer_same_type_mech_rank10 HIGH→MEDIUM question.
learnings.implication: Tier rule calibration is eval-framework-sensitive. Confirms h964 conclusion that h904/h908 directional decisions hold but absolute magnitudes shifted enough to warrant per-rule re-audit.

learnings.learning: Principled spelling-variant aliasing covers only ~8% of the disease-name coverage gap. The real gap is name-granularity mismatch between mesh_mappings (mostly MeSH canonical short form) and disease_names (DRKG-side canonical, often more specific). Less-specific-prefix fallback is DANGEROUS: 43% of its hits produce wrong ids. Always validate alias hits against an authoritative id source.
learnings.implication: When the question is 'can X mapping recover the Y missing entries?', validate every X hit against an authoritative source (here: disease_names). An 'alias' that points to a different id than ground truth is worse than no alias at all.

learnings.learning: Post-hoc tier-remap simulations miss promotion-cascade effects. Demoting HIGH→MEDIUM exposes predictions to MEDIUM+STRONG_EVIDENCE→GOLDEN promotion at line 4959, which can dominate the net tier impact. Simulation predicted +1.44pp HIGH but real was +0.5pp HIGH and +4.0pp GOLDEN because STRONG-lit cancer_same_type_mech_rank10 preds cascaded to GOLDEN.
learnings.implication: Future HIGH→MEDIUM or MEDIUM→X demotion audits must model the full post-processing pipeline (transe_medium_promotion, literature_strong_promotion, literature_weak_demotion) — or run actual predictor code on the modified rule — not just a post-hoc label remap on cached counters.

learnings.learning: Per-category biologic prior is too coarse to drive precision-aware demotion. kNN already concentrates biologics in immunology/cancer/endocrine; remaining biologics in low-prior categories are mostly real hits when present. Category-level demotion is precision-neutral or negative, never +2pp.
learnings.implication: Per-disease (not per-category) biologic priors derived from kNN neighbors are needed. h990 will test that. Also: precision pivots for biologics likely need to operate on the SMALL-MOLECULE side, not biologics — bio_r30=30% > overall_r30=20%, biologics OVERPERFORM.

learnings.learning: Even the finest-grained per-disease neighbor-derived biologic prior cannot drive a precision lift via top-30 demotion+refill. The kNN rank 31-200 tail is uniform-quality — replacing in-top-30 biologics with rank-31+ non-biologics is precision-NEUTRAL because the replacements hit at the same background rate. h990 + h953 jointly close the "biologic in/out shuffle" precision-pivot family.
learnings.implication: Precision lifts must operate INSIDE the rank 1-30 window via score differentiation (re-ranking), not via in-out exchange. h993/h994 will test that direction. The strict prior=0 filter is a safe a-priori invariant that could be used as a documentation/annotation column without harm.

learnings.learning: Biologic target-family-match is a genuine cross-drug signal (4.22x LOO in autoimmune, 5.67-24.22x in cancer/cv/hematological) but cannot operate as an in/out filter: half the hits (16/32 autoimmune) are target-unique in bio_gt, so filtering would cost 50% of biologic recall. Same failure mode as h957. h1000 (in-window re-rank) and h1001 (annotation column) are the viable surfaces.
learnings.implication: Any filter that REMOVES biologic candidates based on bio_gt-referenced signals will fail the -2pp bio_r30 gate because the set of biologic hits is half target-unique. Future biologic precision work must use re-rank (keep all 30 slots) or deliverable annotation (no ranking change).

learnings.learning: Neighbor-augmented bio_gt rescues only 6.2% of autoimmune unique-target biologic hits (1/16). Proves that 50% of autoimmune biologic HITS are target-unique at the disease-neighborhood level — structural cap on filter-form biologic precision improvements at -50pp bio_r30.
learnings.implication: Close filter-form biologic precision pivots as a family. Closed: h953/h957/h990/h995/h1002. Focus on in-window re-rank (h994/h1000) and deliverable annotation (h1001/h1003).

learnings.learning: In-window ±1 biologic rank shift is too diffuse to move tier precision. Only 1.7% of biologic preds cross tier-rule boundaries (which sit at ranks 5/10/15/20). The filter-form biologic precision family (h953, h957, h990, h995, h1000, h1002) remains closed. Score-perturbation in-window without in/out exchange DOES preserve bio_r30 exactly (by construction) — so the approach is safe — but the tier rules aren't granular enough at ±1 rank to register a lift.
learnings.implication: Future precision pivots on biologics must either: (a) use larger rank shifts (h1005) or boundary-targeted shifts (h1006) to increase boundary crossings per shift; (b) exploit per-category signal asymmetry (h1008); or (c) abandon tier-rule surface in favor of deliverable annotation columns (h1003, h1007). The 'in-window re-rank via score perturbation' mechanism is sound — failure was in magnitude, not principle.

learnings.learning: In-window biologic score-perturbation re-rank fails at BOTH ±1.5 and ±3.5. Magnitude is not the bottleneck — signal density is. Only 22% of biologics have target_match_loo_neighbor=True (bump candidates); 78% are False (demote candidates, most already at LOW/FILTER going to FILTER). High-precision promotions from biologic match=True are rare (4-6 hits across 5 seeds at 100% precision) — numerically too small to lift 53-slot GOLDEN or 213-slot HIGH tiers. Demotion side works as intended (legitimate LOW→FILTER per rank>20 rule) but cannot LIFT any tier.
learnings.implication: Abandon score-perturbation re-rank as a tier-precision surface. Move to: (1) boundary-targeted shift (h1006) that only activates near rank 5/10/15/20 thresholds to maximize boundary-crossing rate; (2) deliverable annotation column (h1003, h1007) that doesn't touch tier assignment. Score-perturbation is mechanically safe (bio_r30 preserved) but cannot lift tiers because the match=True bump signal is too concentrated in few biologics.

learnings.learning: Known-indication flag (drug_id in self.ground_truth.get(disease_id)) is a clean carve-out signal for FILTER-demoting rules. 3 rules correctly exempted; safety filters (inverse indication, rank>20, no targets) intentionally NOT exempted. 543/779 remaining known-indication FILTER cases are rank>20 — genuine kNN mis-ranking, not a rule fix.
learnings.implication: The rank>20 structural floor is the dominant remaining source of paper-visible FILTER misfires on FDA-approved indications. Not fixable by tier rules; only by improving the underlying ranker (h1200 supervised GNN). Also: every new tier-demoting rule should explicitly decide whether to exempt known indications before shipping.

learnings.learning: Paper Section 3.5 crown-jewel table conflates RCT cohort with RCT outcome in at least one row (Dantrolene: 'heart failure' cohort, 'VT reduction' outcome). The model correctly identifies the VT signal at rank 34 but is FILTER-tier because of the structural rank>20 kNN floor, not a rule misfire. No code change required; paper errata only.
learnings.implication: h1107 queued to audit every row of Section 3.5 — other rows may have the same conflation. Also h1106 queued to clean up drug_cancer_types artifacts (Dantrolene incorrectly has 'solid_tumor' despite no cancer role).

learnings.learning: Paper Section 3.5 'retrospectively corroborated' claim holds for only 1 of 5 rows (Rituximab->MS). Dantrolene, Lovastatin, Pitavastatin, Empagliflozin are ABSENT from their claimed disease's top predictions. For Empagliflozin the model surfaces 3 correct FDA indications (T2D/HF/CKD) but all at rank 21-52 -> FILTER via rank_over_20. Paper credibility issue at crown-jewel level.
learnings.implication: Recommend Paper v2 Option A revision: collapse Section 3.5 to one row (Rituximab->MS) and move others to supplementary 'prior art' table. The Empagliflozin case is the cleanest h1103 (rank>20 audit) candidate and the strongest argument for the h1200 supervised-GNN pivot.

learnings.learning: 74% of the 543 rank>20 known-indication misfires have mech=False — sparse DRKG edge history, not a rule bug. 62% are at ranks 21-25 (just outside the threshold). Top clusters: other_sm x infectious (66), other_sm x autoimmune (41), biologic_mab x autoimmune (28). The SGLT2 family (Empagliflozin, ~7 cases) matches h1107's observation.
learnings.implication: h1200 supervised GNN should upweight these 543 pairs during training (h1110 proposed). Biologic_mab x autoimmune (28 cases) is a natural Ryland review packet (h1111).
